Users are now able to learn Hadith knowledge using their day-to-day conversational language as a medium of interaction. Identified future work includes the knowledge base expansion and multilingual support implementation into the system. In addition to the Sahih Muslim and Syarah Sahih Muslim, other major Hadith collections, Quranic verses, and their interpretations should be integrated to make the system more comprehensive for Islamic knowledge as a whole. Multilingual support could also be considered to expand the chatbot to a more diverse group of users. Overall, this project has demonstrated the effectiveness of Hadith chatbot using LLM in enhancing accessibility and understanding of Hadith knowledge by removing the process of static keyword searches and search results skimming.

titulo: B-RAG: A Retrieval Augmented Generation Based AI System for Educational Question Answering from Bangla Textbook in Bangla
autores: M. S. A. Khan; M. S. A. Khan
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: Bangladesh’s education system heavily relies on National Curriculum and Textbook Board (NCTB) resources, which serve as the primary knowledge base for millions of students across the country. However, digital tools for interactive learning in Bangla remain limited, particularly in supporting direct question answering from these textbooks. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) enhances educational chatbots by improving accuracy and contextual relevance while mitigating hallucinations in large language models. Although RAG systems have been applied globally in language learning, programming, health, and legal education, no system currently addresses Bangla textbook question answering. To address this, we propose B-RAG, a RAGpowered chatbot that retrieves and generates accurate Bangla responses from NCTB content. The system indexes textbook content into a vector database, performs semantic retrieval, and generates responses via a large language model, deployed through a Streamlit interface with FastAPI. Evaluation using MultiClassification, Token-Similarity, and Token-Level F1 metrics shows high retrieval accuracy, strong linguistic alignment, and precise answer generation, demonstrating B-RAG’s potential for context-aware educational support in Bangla.

titulo: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Large Language Model For Educational Chatbot
autores: L. Danuarta; V. C. Mawardi; V. Lee
venue: 2024 Ninth International Conference on Informatics and Computing (ICIC)
abstract: In the digital age, educational chatbots are increasingly essential for providing personalized learning experience. This study explores the potential of the Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) method to enhanced the performance of educational chatbots. By integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) with real-time data retrieval from external sources, the RAG approach improves the accuracy, relevance, and safety of chatbot responses. Tested using an Indonesian elementary school e-book dataset on Physical Education, Sports, and Health (PJOK), the RAG model demonstrated significantly improvements in generating accurate and contextually appropriate answers while minimizing harmful content. The model achieved a mean context precision of 0.69, context recall of 0.70, faithfulness of 0.60, answer relevancy of 0.86, and harmfulness reduction to 0.26. The findings underscore the effectiveness of RAG advancing educational chatbot performance.

titulo: Dynamic Retrieval Augmented Generation for Enterprise Knowledge Intelligence Systems using Large Language Models
autores: C. Thumma; A. S. Sribhashyam; C. Tumma; N. Suresh
venue: 2026 International Conference on Intelligent and Sustainable AI Systems (ICOSAAS)
abstract: To address the difficulty faced by university faculty and students in obtaining useful information from massive campus data, this paper proposes an intelligent campus question-and-answer (Q&A) system based on dynamic retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) technology, using campus administrative knowledge as the data source. The system integrates large language models (LLMs) with domain-specific professional knowledge, leveraging the Campus All-in-One project as a foundation. It constructs a campus knowledge base that includes administrative guides, frequently asked questions, and regulatory documents as an external data corpus. By applying the Infinity database, designed specifically for dynamic RAG applications, and employing prompt engineering, the model’s ability to generate accurate and context-aware answers is enhanced. Through this dynamic RAG-based approach tailored for the education domain, the system provides users with interactive access to a wide range of campus administrative information, helping to resolve common issues, simplify inquiry processes for teachers and students, and reduce the workload of campus management.

titulo: Enhancing Cancer Information Access with a Retrieval-Augmented Generation Chatbot
autores: K. A. Wira Santosa; C. Huda
venue: 2025 11th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: Cancer is one of the leading causes of death worldwide, with millions of new cases and deaths reported each year. As cancer-related research and guidelines progress at a fast pace, both patients and healthcare professionals face difficulties in accessing trustworthy and up-to-date information. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture is introduced using the LangChain framework to solve this problem by combining generative capabilities of LLM and vector-based retrieval. The knowledge used in this chatbot consists of cancer-related articles from NIH and hundreds of research abstracts related to cancer from PubMed. Users can ask the chatbot about cancer-related questions, such as symptoms, diagnosis, and treatment. The chatbot generates responses using the retrieved information from the vector database and provides the retrieved sources. RAGAS framework and 50 questions from the MedQuAD dataset are used to evaluate the chatbot’s performance in faithfulness, context precision, answer relevancy, and context recall. The retrieval showed robust performance, but the generation component still struggles. This can be further improved by using pre-trained LLMs and better prompting techniques. Future work will focus on developing better knowledge base and better chunking strategies.

titulo: Athena: A GenAI-Powered Programming Tutor Based on Open-Source LLM
autores: Y. Lin; M. F. Ferdous Khan; K. Sakamura
venue: 2025 1st International Conference on Consumer Technology (ICCT-Pacific)
abstract: With the rapid growth of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), it is important to find ways to utilize them for academic advantage. GenAI tools embody immense potential in providing personalized feedback to students any time anywhere, and hence can provide a reliable helping hand to teachers who often experience burnout in large classes and are burdened with administrative tasks. While current GenAI tools like ChatGPT are helpful, they occasionally offer misinformation - a phenomenon known as hallucination, undermine critical thinking by providing direct answers to questions, and, as paid services, can further widen the digital divide. Against the backdrop of these problems, this research introduces Athena, a GenAI programming mentor based on an open-source large language model (LLM), constructed to guide programming learners to think critically and provide reliable information leveraging retrieval augmented generation. Its impact on learning outcomes was measured by feedback from programming students. Most students have given a positive response, saying that their motivation to keep learning and their confidence in their abilities have increased. These results imply that having a reliable AI mentor that can guide students at all times can have a positive impact in self-directed learning process.

titulo: OphthaRAG: A Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework for Enhanced Eye Disease Diagnosis Support and Question Answering
autores: U. Kaur; D. M. Chakkaravarthy
venue: 2026 International Conference on Advancements in Smart, Secure and Intelligent Computing (ASSIC)
abstract: The integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) into healthcare holds transformative potential, yet their application in highly specialized fields like ophthalmology is constrained by hallucination and domain-specific knowledge deficits. To address this, we introduce OphthaRAG, a comprehensive Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework engineered specifically for ophthalmological diagnosis support and question answering. Grounded in a meticulously curated knowledge base encompassing the Basic and Clinical Science Course (BCSC), clinical guidelines, and peer-reviewed literature, OphthaRAG employs a robust two-stage retrieval pipeline utilizing bi-encoder and cross-encoder architectures. We rigorously evaluate the framework using open-source LLMs, including Llama-3-70B and Mixtral-8x7B, on standardized benchmarks such as OphthoQuestions. Our experimental results reveal substantial improvements: OphthaRAG boosts diagnostic accuracy by 15% to 25% over zero-shot baselines and drastically mitigates hallucination rates, improving context faithfulness by 43%. By enabling traceable, evidence-based reasoning, OphthaRAG bridges the critical gap between theoretical LLM capabilities and the strict reliability requirements of clinical practice.

titulo: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Based Large Language Model Chatbot for Improving Diagnosis for Physical and Mental Health
autores: Y. B. Sree; A. Sathvik; D. S. Hema Akshit; O. Kumar; B. S. Pranav Rao
venue: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: Chatbot integration in the medical domain results in improved accessibility to healthcare information and services with enhanced patient query communication and patient education. The proposed work is a novel approach to Health Care chatbot named MEDGPT. The model is developed using the Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework integrated with external data sources such as PDF documents, CSV files, and PubMed documents related to Health Care. It combines a retriever component of the architecture to fetch relevant information from external sources and a generator component to craft contextually appropriate responses using Large Language Model (LLM's). The architecture employed tools and agents in order to generate response from multiple external sources. Tools are specialized for each data source and are designed to extract relevant information based on user queries. Agents are components within the chatbot architecture that handle different aspects of logical reasoning and decision making. When a user query, requires information from an external data source, the corresponding agent invokes the appropriate retrieval tool. Once the data is processed, it is integrated into the chatbot's knowledge base using the RAG framework. The RAG framework combines the retrieved data with the chatbot's language generation capabilities to craft contextually appropriate responses to user queries. Through extensive testing and evaluation, the chatbot achieved significant improvements in user satisfaction, response accuracy, and engagement, showcasing the potential of the RAG framework in leveraging external data sources for intelligent conversational agents in Health Care. The proposed framework enhanced the RAG based LLM chatbot's capabilities to provide relevant and accurate responses to user queries related to Health Care with respected Physical and Mental health.

titulo: Improving Cost Efficiency in Medical Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Adaptive Query Routing
autores: K. -C. Chang; A. S. M
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics - Taiwan (ICCE-Taiwan)
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown strong potential in medical question answering, but their challenge to generate hallucinated or outdated information poses serious risks in clinical settings. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) mitigates this issue by grounding responses in external knowledge; however, indiscriminate retrieval can introduce noise and degrade performance when internal knowledge is sufficient. This paper presents a selective retrieval strategy that dynamically determines whether external retrieval is required. A fine-tuned LLM is used as a query routing mechanism to choose between direct generation and retrievalaugmented generation, combined with a stratified retrieval pipeline over trusted medical sources. Experiments on MedQA-USMLE and MMLU-Medical show accuracies of 70.46% and 77.59% using LLaMA-3 8B, improving over direct generation by 8.72 and 5.60 percentage points, respectively.

titulo: Enhancing Medical Question-Answering Chatbot with RAG-Based Retrieval and Summarization
autores: O. T. -C. Chen; C. -H. Chang
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics - Taiwan (ICCE-Taiwan)
abstract: This work proposes a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)-based medical question-answering chatbot designed for resource-constrained platforms. The proposed Medical Retrieval & Summarization (MRS) module integrates dense passage retrieval for semantically rich search, PEGASUS for summarizing retrieved content, and a refinement module called Gateformer to enhance summary-question alignment. This design reduces redundancy and emphasizes key information, enabling LLAMA-3 8B to produce high-quality answers without fine-tuning. Experiments on PubMedQA demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves 74.00% accuracy, outperforming BM25 + prompt-based LLM and narrowing the gap between small and large-scale Large Language Models (LLMs). These results highlight the effectiveness of our MRS in optimizing retrieval and summarization, enhancing small LLMs for specific applications.

titulo: A Client-Server Based Educational Chatbot for Academic Institutions
autores: R. P. Richard; E. Veemaraj; J. M. Thomas; J. Mathew; C. Stephen; R. S. Koshy
venue: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Technologies (CONIT)
abstract: The use of Generative AI applications in academia, such as ChatGPT, Bard and Perplexity among others is growing at a rapid pace. With its rise, certain ramifications are being felt in regards to the quality and correctness of knowledge and output of these apps. This is detrimental to the process of learning and understanding subject matter in relevant context. In order to stop this issue in its tracks, a solution must be identified, built, tested and deployed so that students will get reliable outputs from trusted sources. This research analyses and describes a sample architecture as well as implementation for such a solution. It incorporates the latest in AI research and development, such as the Large Language Model Mixture of Experts (MoE) architecture as well as a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) with a vector store to use trusted documents such as presentation files, PDF handouts and more from instructors. This is used to add context to the request to the Large Language Model and enrich the understanding as well as response of the model. Apart from this, the application is packaged into a server that can be run on the intranet, as well as deployed for public access. A frontend client page is served to the user, and communicates with the server for all its functioning.

titulo: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Driven Question Answering in Traditional Chinese Medicinal Diets
autores: C. Zeng; X. Wu; W. Lin
venue: 2025 IEEE Cyber Science and Technology Congress (CyberSciTech)
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated great potential in open-domain question answering. However, their generated content is often affected by hallucinations and outdated knowledge, limiting their reliability in specialized domains. To improve the quality of question answering in the field of traditional Chinese medicinal diets, this study designs and implements a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)-based intelligent QA system. Built upon a corpus of medicinal diet literature, the system employs tool-augmented LLMs to automatically extract knowledge triples, and constructs an efficient retrieval mechanism through semantic clustering and Bloom filters. On top of this, a personalized response agent is introduced to dynamically integrate retrieval results based on the user’s body constitution and query intent, enabling the model to generate responses more tailored to individual needs. Experiments evaluate the performance differences of several mainstream models in both knowledge extraction and answer generation, providing practical insights and technical references for building trustworthy, scalable, and personalized QA services in the medicinal diet domain.

titulo: An Evidence-Grounded Multi-Stage Retrieval-Augmented Framework for Multimodal Medical Question Answering
autores: K. Sharma; S. Srivastava; S. Sahrawat; A. Singhal
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on AI Engineering and Innovations (AIEI)
abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based medical question answering systems often produce fluent answers, but they lack clear grounding, source traceability, and verification, which limits their reliability for clinical exploration of knowledge and medical education. By conditioning responses on external evidence, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) mitigates these constraints. However, most current medical RAG techniques rely on shallow pipelines and single-source retrieval, leave them susceptible to topic drift, noisy context, and unsupported generation. This paper proposes a multi-stage, evidence-grounded RAG framework that explicitly models retrieval quality, evidence sufficiency, and grounding verification through a five-stage orchestrated pipeline consisting of multi-source retrieval from PubMed and NCBI Bookshelf, cross-encoder reranking, sentence-level evidence distillation, gated follow-up retrieval, grounded answer generation using a locally deployed LLM (Ollama), and post-generation grounding verification with safe regeneration. To facilitate multimodal reasoning and guarantee that all medical explanations are produced solely by the text-based RAG pipeline, the framework further allows clinical documents provided by the user and vision-derived summaries. ResNet-18 models trained and assessed on common MedMNIST benchmarks are used to create vision components, which are only merged after independent validation. In comparison to LLM-only and single-source RAG baselines, quantitative evaluation on curated medical queries shows improved evidence-to-answer ratio, traceability coverage, and grounding pass rate while also offering competitive latency and stable behavior. These findings emphasize how crucial explicit orchestration and verification are to providing accurate answers to medical questions.

titulo: LLM-Based Personalized Medical Chatbot Enhancing Credibility and User-Centric Healthcare
autores: S. P; K. K. G; T. Y
venue: 2026 9th International Conference on Trends in Electronics and Informatics (ICOEI)
abstract: Current medical chatbots often lack credibility, personalization, and contextual awareness, which limits their reliability in delivering accurate healthcare guidance. They typically provide generic responses without considering individual health records, thereby increasing the risk of misinformation. This paper presents a credible and personalized healthcare assistant powered by Large Language Models (LLMs) that generates context-aware, user-specific medical responses. The system integrates Optical Character Recognition (OCR) to extract structured data from user-uploaded prescriptions and diagnostic reports, which are stored in a database. A Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture is employed to enhance response accuracy by combining user-specific data with relevant knowledge retrieved from external sources, specifically the Gale Encyclopedia of Medicine, represented as embeddings in a vector database. Queries are processed using the Mistral model, which leverages both user data and retrieved context to produce accurate and trustworthy medical insights. By uniting OCR-based document understanding, user-centric data modeling, and external knowledge retrieval, the proposed system provides reliable, scalable, and personalized healthcare support.

titulo: Towards a Safe and Trustworthy LLM-RAG Chatbot for Hemodialysis Patient Education: Design, Implementation, and Preliminary Evaluation
autores: P. K. Putra; E. Nurfadhilah; S. Pebiana; E. Prakasa
venue: 2025 International Conference on Computer, Control, Informatics and its Applications (IC3INA)
abstract: The increasing demand for accurate, timely, and personalized medical information in healthcare, especially for chronic disease management such as hemodialysis, has prompted the development of advanced technological solutions. This paper presents Chatbot Lisa, a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (LLM-RAG) system designed to assist hemodialysis patients by providing relevant and accurate medical information. The focus of this paper is on the system architecture, highlighting the use of the Django framework for the frontend, Sanic for asynchronous request handling, and ChromaDB for semantic retrieval. The chatbot engine leverages the best model, Sahabat AI LLM Model with BGE-M3 embedding model. Additional features, such as user authentication and continuous feedback mechanisms, are included to improve the user experience and support iterative system refinement.

titulo: Smart Educational Chatbot Using Natural Language Processing and Artificial Intelligence
autores: T. M; S. C. C; S. M; S. H. R; B. H. M. Kumar
venue: 2026 4th International Conference on Knowledge Engineering and Communication Systems (ICKECS)
abstract: In the rapidly evolving landscape of higher education, institutions are constantly seeking innovative digital solutions to streamline administrative processes and enhance student engagement. Prospective and current students often encounter significant friction when attempting to access timely and accurate information regarding admissions, curriculum details, fee structures, and campus facilities. Traditional enquiry methods, such as manual help desks and static web portals, frequently suffer from limited availability, information latency, and human error. To address these critical challenges, this paper presents the design, implementation, and comprehensive evaluation of a "Smart Educational College Chatbot," specifically tailored for Sri Jagadguru Chandrashekaranatha Swamiji Institute of Technology (SJCIT). The proposed system utilizes a novel hybrid architecture that synergizes rule-based local logic with the advanced generative capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs), specifically integrating Google’s Gemini 1.5 Flash. To ensure high fidelity and domain specificity, the chatbot employs a robust Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework, grounding its responses in a verifiable institutional knowledge base. Furthermore, the system features novel utility-enhancing modules such as "Document Droid" for automated certificate generation and a "Grade Calculator," alongside comprehensive voice-to-text accessibility features. Experimental results indicate that the chatbot significantly reduces administrative workload and improves information retrieval efficiency by over 40% compared to traditional manual methods.

titulo: Design and Implementation of an AI Agent for Educational Applications via Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Local Language Models on Messaging Platforms
autores: A. Pechbooranin; C. Inchana; V. Charoensak; T. Termprommarat; K. Chamniprasart; J. Varagul
venue: 2025 17th International Conference on Information Technology and Electrical Engineering (ICITEE)
abstract: This study presents the design and implementation of a curriculum-aligned question-answering agent tailored for educational applications, leveraging Retrieval-Augmented Generation with local deployment of large language models. The system integrates domain-specific instructional data-including course handbooks, program learning outcomes, and class schedules-into a Chroma vector database, enabling semantic retrieval via embedding-based similarity search. LLaMA 3.1, deployed locally through Ollama, is used as the language generation model. The framework is implemented using the LangChain orchestration library and exposed to users through the LINE messaging platform, facilitating mobile-friendly interaction in real-time. A benchmark dataset of 200 curriculum-related frequently asked questions was compiled and annotated to evaluate system performance. Experimental results show an accuracy of 90% on the training subset and 80% on the held-out test set. ChatGPT40 (OpenAI) was used as the baseline for comparative evaluation, and error analysis highlights challenges with ambiguous queries and long-range dependencies. Performance profiling reveals inference latency of approximately 2.1 seconds per response on consumer-grade hardware. This work demonstrates the feasibility and effectiveness of deploying lightweight yet accurate QA agents using open-source LLMs in constrained environments.

titulo: Evaluation and Optimization of LLM and RAG Components for a Post-Operative Oral Surgery Consultation Chatbot
autores: S. Lochanachit; P. Bunlaue; C. Kaewmuneechoke; N. Wilairatanaporn; V. Trachoo; K. Warin; P. Pavarangkoon
venue: 2025 25th International Conference on Control, Automation and Systems (ICCAS)
abstract: The increasing demand for dental services highlights the need for efficient post-operative oral surgery consultations. Many patients experience anxiety due to limited knowledge of oral care and treatment. This study introduces a chatbot prototype integrating Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and Large Language Models (LLMs) to provide accurate, context-aware responses. The research evaluates various LLMs, embedding models, and chunking techniques to enhance chatbot performance. The multilingual-e5-large embedding model excelled in retrieval tasks due to its multilingual training, instruction tuning, and contrastive pre-training, ensuring high retrieval precision. The Hybrid Chunking method was selected for its ability to segment text contextually, combining Markdown-based, token-based, and semantic segmentation for optimal chunk relevance. The Llama3.3 (70B) model was chosen for its superior fluency, relevance, and ability to handle complex dependencies. The results demonstrate that combining the multilingual-e5-large embedding model, Hybrid Chunking technique, and Llama3.3 (70B) model improves retrieval precision, response accuracy, and relevance, enhancing patient care and operational effectiveness of dental staffs.

titulo: IRG-RAG: An Iterative Reflective Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation Method for Chinese Medicine
autores: J. Zhang; L. Ma; H. Liu; B. An; Q. Sun
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Bioinformatics and Biomedicine (BIBM)
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) hold significant potential in the medical domain but are hindered by the “hallucination” phenomenon, where generated content may be plausible but factually incorrect. Retrieval-Augmented Generation has emerged as an effective paradigm to mitigate this by integrating external knowledge, and gradually migrates to storing and retrieving relevant information within graph structure. Currently, most Graph RAG methods in medical domain face critical limitations such as semantic poverty of the graph and the fragility of the retrieval process. We propose IRG-RAG, an Iterative Reflective Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation framework tailored for Chinese medical question-answering, focuses on addressing these two key challenges. Our framework introduces a knowledge-enhanced graph construction method, enriching edges with contextual descriptions to endow the graph with richer semantic information. Additionally, we propose an iterative reflective retrieval strategy, which dynamically travels on the graph to retrieve relevant information, backtracks from ineffective paths to reduce noise, and incorporates negative feedback to guide subsequent explorations, mimicking humanlike problem-solving. Experiments on CMExam and CMB-Exam datasets demonstrate that our method significantly enhances the reliability of the model's answer, offering a robust solution to hallucination in domain-specific applications. Codes and data will be available at https://github.com/Damon1Zhang/IRG-RAG.

titulo: AI-Driven Knowledge Retrieval for Medical Question-Answering Using Large Language Models and Retrieval-Augmented Generation
autores: A. R. Faridi; Keshvi; F. Masood
venue: 2026 6th International Conference on Multimedia, Signal Processing and Communication Technologies (IMPACT)
abstract: Precise medical question-and-answer (QA) systems are essential for clinical decision-making, medical education, and patient care because they provide quick and precise medical information. With immense progress made, high accuracy in medical QA continues to be challenging due to biomedical information complexity and specialty. To solve these issues, this study systematically investigates other state-of-the-art Large Language Model (LLM) prompting strategies as well as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) methods. The main objective of this paper is to thoroughly investigate and contrast the performance of several methods on the MedMCQA dataset-a well-known medical QA benchmark having about $\mathbf{4, 1 0 0}$ multiple-choice questions on diverse medical topics-such as zero-shot prompting, Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting, TF-IDF with XGBoost baseline, fine-tuned PubMed-BERT, and three RAG variants (Naive RAG, Query Expansion, and Answer Expansion). Our results show significant performance differences between methods. The standard TF-IDF+XGBoost baseline achieved low accuracy $(32.07 \%)$, while fine-tuned PubMedBERT boosted to $\mathbf{4 4. 0 \%}$. LLM-based prompting yielded significant improvements, particularly for OpenAI's GPT-4 in a zero-shot setup $(80.13 \%)$. But RAG methods significantly surpassed all other methodology, Answer Expansion-based RAG achieving the highest accuracy of about 85%. This research highlights the high promise of retrieval-enhanced methods in medical QA, calling for broader adoption and continued research on RAG frameworks, specifically those incorporating Answer Expansion, in clinical informatics applications.

titulo: A Concise GNN-LLM Alignment Framework for Knowledge-Enhanced Medical Question Answering
autores: C. Song; X. Chen; H. Zhang; R. Hu; W. Liang
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Bioinformatics and Biomedicine (BIBM)
abstract: Knowledge Graph based Retrieval-Augmented Generation (KG-RAG) technology is an effective method to improve the performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) in medical question answering tasks. However, there is an inherent difference between structured knowledge graphs and sequential LLMs. The existing method of converting triples of knowledge graph into text through predefined templates leads to loss of structural information and excessive context length, resulting in alignment difficulties between the two. In this paper, we propose a GNN-LLM Aligned Medical knowledge QuestionAnswering model (GLAM-QA). The model first pretrains a GNN to extract structural information from the knowledge graph, realizes the interactive fusion of graph representations and LLM vocabulary embeddings through a cross attention layer, and then generates graph tokens via a projector for input to the LLM. It can retain graph structural information without finetuning the LLM and provide accurate and concise answers. Experiments on three public datasets show that compared with five comparative algorithms, the proposed GLAM-QA achieves better performance in BertScore, F1-Score, and BLEU-1 metrics. This research provides an effective solution to the alignment problem between knowledge graphs and LLMs, and improves the accuracy and practicality of medical question answering systems.

titulo: MediBot: AI-Powered Healthcare Chatbot with Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Accurate Medical Response
autores: S. K. Mishra; M. Singh; S. Saravanan; T. R. Kumar; P. Robert; S. Sivakumar
venue: 2026 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Automation for Sustainable Solutions (ICASS)
abstract: The given work is an introduction to MediBot, which is an AI-driven healthcare chatbot designed using the Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) model of providing relevant and contextual medical information. By combining large language model generation with semantic document retrieval, the system bases responses on medical literature that is proven to be valid thus minimizing hallucinations and enhancing factual accuracy. Medical records are domain specific documents that are embedded and indexed to enable easy retrieval and the context of the retrieved is integrated with user queries to give informed responses. MediBot is implemented as a framework of real-time interactive application, which indicates the practical relevance of retrieval-enhanced large language models in virtual medical consultation and delivery of health information. The given strategy identifies the promise of the RAG-based systems to deliver scalable, reliable, and trustful AI-assisted healthcare support.

titulo: An On-Premise Multilingual Academic Chatbot using Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Context-Aware Memory for University Assistance
autores: M. S. Yaswanth; K. Sai Amar Durgesh; M. H. Vardhan; S. Riyaz
venue: 2026 7th International Conference on Smart Systems and Inventive Technology (ICSSIT)
abstract: Universities now use Large Language Models (LLMs) to transform their processes for managing student information. The paper introduces an upgraded chatbot system for Narasaraopeta Engineering College (NEC) which extends previous on-premise LLM chatbot research by providing four new functions. The system uses (1) Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to create citation-based responses through LlamaIndex and ChromaDB, (2) Context Memory which maintains conversation flow during multiple dialogue exchanges, (3) Voice Input through OpenAI Whisper Speech-to-Text (STT) technology, and (4) Multilingual Support which covers English and these seven languages: Hindi, Telugu, Tamil, Kannada, and Malayalam through IndicNLP. The system tested 60 benchmark questions across four academic categories which included regulations and examination policies and fee structures and multilingual queries and achieved 96.7% overall accuracy with sub-second text response times and 1.0–1.4 second voice response times. The system operates entirely on-premise through Docker which safeguards institutional data privacy while eliminating the need for recurring cloud API expenses. The upcoming development will create Emotion-Aware AI, FAQ Auto-Learning, Student Portal Integration, and a Mobile Application.

titulo: QuickAid: A Hybrid RAG and LLM Framework for Improving Chatbot Accuracy and Relevance in First-Aid Guidance
autores: D. Shikha; S. Bansal; A. Raman; S. Sharma
venue: 2025 International Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (ICCCT)
abstract: India is facing significant healthcare issues, including a doctor-patient ratio of 1:836, delayed emergency response times, and terribly limited medical infrastructure in rural areas where 65% of the population reside, while healthcare facilities number only 25%. With overcrowded hospitals dealing with routine non-emergency cases, proper first aid counsel could help in such cases. Also, in case of emergencies step by step first aid guidance help patients to save their life by managing critical situations, like cardiac arrest, choking, or severe bleeding before reaching hospitals. To bridge the healthcare gap, there is a need of medical chatbot that provides immediate, cost effective and multimodal emergency guidance especially in rural areas. The rapid advancements in artificial intelligence(AI) have significantly transformed healthcare applications, particularly in the development of medical chatbots. To create an intelligent First Aid Medical Chatbot, this study proposes QuickAid, a hybrid approach that integrates Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and Large Language Models (LLMs). RAG improves the ability of the chatbot to provide accurate, real-time first aid advice by retrieving relevant medical knowledge from authoritative and evidence-based sources and combining it with generative AI capabilities. This ensures that users receive accurate, contextually relevant, and timely emergency support. The dataset is designed to cover essential first aid requirements, including choking, headaches, and other medical emergencies. The chatbot facilitates multimodal interaction through both text and audio for better accessibility. Its hybrid strategy helps to lower the risk of errors by employing structured retrieval. QuickAid's effectiveness is supported by a BLEU score of 0.87 and ROUGE scores of 0.92 (ROUGE-1), 0.85 (ROUGE-2), and 0.91 (ROUGE-L), reflecting its high accuracy and fluency.

titulo: Enhancing Student Support in TNE of Lingshui via an AI-Powered RAG Chatbot
autores: X. Wu; Y. Sheng
venue: 2026 4th UK-China Teaching, Learning, and Educational Technology (TILE-TEC)
abstract: In the Transnational Education (TNE) context, scattered sources and multi-institutional governance structures create some hardship for students to access information for support. Aimed at the Hainan Lingshui campus, this paper introduces the development of an AI-driven chatbot prototype based on Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to address some key issues faced by students in obtaining accurate and timely information. The developed prototype adopts an automated multi-source data crawling and processing pipeline, integrates the PostgreSQL vector database, and leverages hybrid retrieval techniques combined with Large Language Models (LLMs) to realize unified integration and accurate response generation. Empirical evaluation demonstrates that the developed system achieves an 87.5% task success rate and reduces information retrieval time by 81.8% compared to traditional manual methods, effectively mitigating hallucinations through a precisely tuned hybrid retrieval strategy.

titulo: HemaRAG: A Retrieval-Augmented Generation System for Medical Question Answering in Hematologic Malignancies
autores: M. E. Chatzimina; N. S. Tachos; D. I. Fotiadis; M. Tsiknakis
venue: 2025 IEEE EMBS International Conference on Biomedical and Health Informatics (BHI)
abstract: Answering complex medical questions requires both reliable information retrieval and the ability to generate responses that are medically accurate and contextually appropriate. In this paper, we present HemaRAG, a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system designed specifically for hematologic malignancies. Our system combines a dense retriever enhanced with biomedical ontologies and a fine-tuned large language model (Gemma 3), trained locally on domain-specific literature and question–answer pairs. To build a robust retrieval base, we enriched PubMed abstracts and curated datasets such as BioASQ and PubMedQA using synonym mappings from MeSH, NCIT, DOID, and UMLS. We used a local vector database to support high-speed semantic search without sharing data externally. Evaluation across both BioASQ and long-form PubMedQA benchmarks showed high semantic accuracy (BERTScore: 87–89%), strong lexical overlap (F1: 49– 52%), and high retrieval performance (Recall@10: 94–96%), despite the challenges posed by free-form medical questions. The system was developed and deployed entirely locally making it suitable for clinical contexts where patient data privacy is essential. In future work, we plan to integrate HemaRAG into an empathetic conversational agent designed to support patients and clinicians in the field of hematologic oncology.

titulo: Document Embeddings Enhance Biomedical Retrieval-Augmented Generation
autores: Y. Kong; Z. Yang; L. Luo; Z. Ding; L. Wang; W. Liu; Y. Zhang; B. Xu; J. Wang; Y. Sun; Z. Zhao; H. Lin
venue: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Bioinformatics and Biomedicine (BIBM)
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) perform well in many NLP tasks but frequently generate inaccurate information in the biomedical domain, due to hallucination issues. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has been introduced to address this issue by integrating external knowledge, enhancing the factual accuracy of outputs. However, naive RAG encounters challenges in effectively utilizing retrieved content, particularly in specialized domains like biomedicine. LLMs often struggle to integrate retrieved content as irrelevant information can interfere with the model’s judgment. Even if relevant documents are retrieved, the model may be unable to accurately comprehend and utilize the domain-specific features due to its inherent knowledge limitations. To overcome these limitations, we propose Document Embeddings Enhanced Biomedical RAG (DEEB-RAG), a framework that incorporates document embeddings along with the original retrieved text. DEEB-RAG uses MedCPT to generate document embeddings and these embeddings are then aligned with the LLM’s semantic space using a two-stage training process on a simple projector. Experimental results on biomedical QA datasets show that DEEB-RAG improves accuracy, with an average performance increase of 2.3% over naive RAG. This demonstrates DEEB-RAG’s ability to mitigate the challenges of utilizing complex biomedical information, thereby enhancing the reliability and effectiveness of LLMs in biomedical domain.

titulo: Design based Retrieval Augmented Generation Oriented Education Chatbot: Edubot
autores: T. Pandey; A. Yadav; J. Sharma; S. Singhal
venue: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advances in Computation, Communication and Information Technology (ICAICCIT)
abstract: Chatbot, a system which focuses on utilizing advanced natural language processing (NLP) techniques. This research aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of Chatbot, including its background, evolution and future application, with the focus mainly on its impact on education. The landscape of scientific research has been transformed by artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning. This research explores OpenAI’s chatbot, which leverages advanced techniques in Natural Language Processing (NLP), Supervised Learning, and Reinforcement Learning to understand and generate text that closely resembles human-written content. As per state-of-art, an interface has been developed along with dataset creation. A small level BOT that would use a self-made database on Pinecone which has been integrated into it. The interface will take the queries from the user and provide a suitable and accurate answer by using the RAG & LLM algorithm.

titulo: SYMPTOMWISE: An AI-Based Symptom Analysis and Triage Chatbot
autores: S. Yadav; R. Shukla; R. Ranjan; K. Singh
venue: 2026 International Conference on Green Technologies and Sustainable Solutions (GTSS)
abstract: More than 3.5 billion people in the world are still affected by healthcare gaps, especially where access to proper medical diagnosis is difficult. This work presents a multimodal AI-powered healthcare chatbot that understands both textual and image-based symptoms. The proposed chatbot, developed using a BioMistral-7B Q4 quantized large language model and further augmented with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), reduces hallucinations and provides medically found responses. Leveraging data from the WHO Global Health Observatory (GHO)[10] and a carefully curated symptomdisease dataset, it delivers trustworthy diagnostic suggestions. Compared to baseline LLMs, the system achieved 95% F1-score in matching symptom-disease, 87% diagnostic accuracy, with an 83% reduction in hallucinations. The results have confirmed the system's ability to deliver equitable and reliable medical care in resource-poor settings.

titulo: An LLM-Driven Chatbot in Higher Education for Databases and Information Systems
autores: A. T. Neumann; Y. Yin; S. Sowe; S. Decker; M. Jarke
venue: IEEE Transactions on Education
abstract: Contribution: This research explores the benefits and challenges of developing, deploying, and evaluating a large language model (LLM) chatbot, MoodleBot, in computer science classroom settings. It highlights the potential of integrating LLMs into LMSs like Moodle to support self-regulated learning (SRL) and help-seeking behavior. Background: Computer science educators face immense challenges incorporating novel tools into LMSs to create a supportive and engaging learning environment. MoodleBot addresses this challenge by offering an interactive platform for both students and teachers. Research Questions: Despite issues like bias, hallucinations, and teachers’ and educators’ resistance to embracing new (AI) technologies, this research investigates two questions: (RQ1) To what extent do students accept MoodleBot as a valuable tool for learning support? (RQ2) How accurately does MoodleBot churn out responses, and how congruent are these with the established course content? Methodology: This study reviews pedagogical literature on AI-driven chatbots and adopts the retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) approach for MoodleBot’s design and data processing. The technology acceptance model (TAM) evaluates user acceptance through constructs like perceived usefulness (PU) and Ease of Use. Forty-six students participated, with 30 completing the TAM questionnaire. Findings: LLM-based chatbots like MoodleBot can significantly improve the teaching and learning process. This study revealed a high accuracy rate (88%) in providing course-related assistance. Positive responses from students attest to the efficacy and applicability of AI-driven educational tools. These findings indicate that educational chatbots are suitable for integration into courses to improve personalized learning and reduce teacher administrative burden, although improvements in automated fact-checking are needed.

titulo: A Knowledge-Enhanced RAG Framework with Re-ranking and Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Cardiovascular Disease Question Answering Using Large Language Models
autores: H. Lu; S. Wang; Z. Liu
venue: 2026 6th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Cardiovascular disease remains a leading cause of global mortality, highlighting the need for intelligent and reliable clinical decision support systems. This paper presents the research and implementation of a cardiovascular question answering system based on Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and Knowledge Graphs (KG). The proposed framework integrates dense and hybrid retrieval, structured knowledge graph reasoning, evidence re-ranking, and chain-of-thought generation to enhance answer accuracy, interpretability, and clinical consistency. Extensive experiments, including survival analysis, multi-type question answering evaluation, ablation studies, and system-level ROC and PR analyses, demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms RAG-only, KG-only, and LLM-only baselines. The results confirm that combining retrieval-based evidence with explicit knowledge graph reasoning provides a robust and explainable solution for cardiovascular clinical question answering.

titulo: Implementation of a RAG-based Knowledge Question Answering System
autores: Y. -C. Lin; K. Pan; D. Vasilisa; T. -W. Kuan; S. Luo; X. Yu
venue: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Digital Media Technology and Social Computing (ICAIDS)
abstract: This study explored an AI teaching assistant system that utilizes LoRA fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs) combined with LangChain technology to improve accuracy in specialized areas like software testing. Employing Agent agents and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), the research demonstrated the feasibility of knowledge-based intelligent question-answering. Initially, relevant technologies such as model fine-tuning and knowledge vector databases were compared, followed by the creation of a software testing dataset from the ISTQB question bank. The system was designed using Qwen-1.8B-Chat and LoRA fine-tuning, with a knowledge vector database built for course information. Agent agents were developed to integrate a local search engine (SearXNG). Testing showed that the fine-tuned LLM significantly improved question-answering accuracy, as measured by BLEU and ROUGE metrics, and the Agent successfully retrieved information from both the search engine and knowledge database. However, the study identified areas for improvement in LLM optimization and knowledge base completeness.

titulo: An Intelligent Retrieval Augmented Generation Chatbot for Contextually-Aware Conversations to Guide High School Students
autores: N. S. Amarnath; R. Nagarajan
venue: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The growth of Large Language Models (LLM) has showcased both their potential and limitations in domain- specific applications. A significant limitation is their tendency to confidently present false information, known as hallucination, which compromises the integrity of their outputs. Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) systems mitigate this by enhancing the Large Language Models' ability to retrieve accurate, source-specific knowledge. Many American students begin preparing for college applications in middle school, seeking guidance on planning their high school years to achieve personal goals. The diversity in students' interests, skills, and circumstances often results in an overwhelming amount of information and advice. This research introduces a novel RAG chatbot designed to provide personalized assistance to high school students using their course guide as the primary source document. By integrating a high school course guide with a RAG system, the chatbot delivers relevant suggestions, helping students navigate their educational paths with greater confidence and precision. This system aims to minimize the risk of hallucination by ensuring that responses are grounded in the accurate and relevant information contained within the course guide. Consequently, it addresses the crucial need for personalized educational planning, enabling students to make informed decisions that align with their unique aspirations and circumstances. This research highlights the transformative potential of RAG systems in educational contexts, offering a reliable tool to support students in their academic and personal growth.

titulo: Towards Developing a Multimodal Chat Assistant for University Stakeholders: RAG-Based Approach
autores: M. A. Hanif Shaikh; A. Al Shafi
venue: 2025 28th International Conference on Computer and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: University stakeholders often face difficulties in accessing timely and reliable information, especially in developing countries, where there are very few intelligent support systems. Existing rule-based chatbots are unable to handle complex, domain-specific queries and are not well-equipped to adapt to evolving institutional policies. As a fill-in-the-gap solution, we present the multimodal university chatbot with retrieval-augmented generation. The system combines the large language model with semantic retrieval to produce context-based responses from institution-centric resources, such as the university handbook. The system accepts text and image queries through the vision-language model and applies quantized inference for rapid deployment on constrained hardware. A scalable backend built with FastAPI, adjoined with a responsive frontend developed with Next.js, ensures real-time usability. Our multimodal evaluation demonstrates that the system maintains strong satisfaction scores across both text and image queries, despite increased response time for visual inputs. Furthermore, quantitative evaluation shows that hallucination is reduced from 31.7% to 6.6% in our proposed RAG-based system, confirming the effectiveness of retrieval grounding.

titulo: TechAssist: A RAG-Based Chatbot for Accessing Technical Information from StackOverflow
autores: R. Vasaniya; M. Visodiya; A. K. Patel
venue: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: This paper presents TechAssist, an advanced artificial intelligence-driven chatbot designed to enhance the learning experience for students and professionals in tech domain. Utilizing the Mistral 7B Instruct model within a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework, TechAssist efficiently retrieves and generates contextually relevant answers to technical queries sourced from the StackOverflow dataset. Implemented with a user-friendly interface using Gradio, the system provides real-time responses, facilitating interactive engagement for users seeking technical support. Evaluation with learners and educators demonstrates the efficacy of TechAssist in delivering accurate and timely information, significantly improving the speed and quality of assistance. The findings indicate that the integration of cutting-edge AI technologies with an intuitive interface result in a more effective learning environment and enhanced user empowerment in addressing technical challenges.

titulo: A Multi-Modal RAG-Based Virtual Health Assistant with 3D Visual Interface
autores: C. -C. Wang; Y. -J. Xie; Y. -J. Hsieh; Y. -J. Huang; P. -Y. Hou
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics - Taiwan (ICCE-Taiwan)
abstract: To address the shortage of medical personnel and the increasing demand for health consultation, we present a multi-modal intelligent health education robot based on Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). The proposed system integrates a large language model with a FAISS vector database, Microsoft Azure Speech Services, and a Unity-based 3D virtual avatar to enable natural speech-based interaction. By grounding responses in a verified internal medical knowledge base, the RAG mechanism improves response reliability and mitigates hallucination issues commonly observed in conventional Large Language Models. The system is designed to provide accessible and easy-to-understand medical guidance, particularly for elderly users and patients with limited literacy, while reducing repetitive educational workloads for medical staff. This work demonstrates the feasibility of applying multi-modal LLM-based systems to practical smart healthcare applications.

titulo: Exploring Opportunities and Addressing Challenges in Designing Knowledge Graph-Enhanced RAG-Based Chatbots for Managing Radiation Toxicity in Cancer Care
autores: U. Bharambe; K. Patil; P. Ingle; U. Bhangale
venue: 2025 International Conference for Artificial Intelligence, Applications, Innovation and Ethics (AI2E)
abstract: Chatbots offer essential support for patients undergoing radiation therapy by providing timely advice, tracking symptoms, and suggesting coping strategies for side effects. They act as a bridge between patients and their care teams, ensuring continuous guidance during treatment. This requires accurate, context-aware, and explainable responses, which is challenging when designing chatbots. New features and capabilities have recently been introduced to chatbot functionality via Large Language Models (LLMs) using technologies such as Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), chatbots can retrieve real-time, relevant information, generating contextually relevant interactions. Traditional LLMs and RAG models still suffer from limitations such as generating hallucinated information and difficulty reasoning over complex relationships. These challenges can be addressed with knowledge graphs, which offer structured, interconnected data representations for chatbots to deliver grounded, understandable responses. Designing a chatbot that integrates knowledge graphs with RAG presents significant opportunities and challenges for developing intelligent, patient-centric conversational systems. Knowledge graphs enhance structured reasoning and accuracy, while RAG supports dynamic and personalized interactions. The paper examines architectural considerations, technological possibilities, and practical applications of such systems, especially in healthcare domains like oncology, where precision and reliability are crucial.

titulo: Enhancing International Graduate Student Experience through AI-Driven Support Systems: A LLM and RAG-Based Approach
autores: B. Saha; U. Saha
venue: 2024 International Conference on Data Science and Its Applications (ICoDSA)
abstract: International graduate students encounter unique challenges that impede their academic and personal success. This paper introduces an AI-powered chatbot designed specifically for these students, utilizing advanced language models and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). Unlike generic solutions, our chatbot is tailored with a dataset curated from Reddit communi-ties frequented by international students, enabling it to provide highly relevant and actionable advice. The system combines GPT-3.5's generative capabilities with precise information retrieval to effectively guide students through academic procedures, cul-tural adjustments, and personal challenges. An evaluation shows that our RAG-enhanced model outperforms standard GPT-3.5, demonstrating significant improvements in response accuracy and relevance. This research not only advances AI applications in student support but also offers practical, real-time aid to enhance international students' educational experiences.

titulo: OYEN: A User-Centric LLM-Based Bilingual Healthcare Chatbot
autores: O. Chin; N. S. Jamil; Z. Zainudin; N. A. Hitam; N. Ibrahim; A. H. Ahmad Sa'ahiry
venue: 2024 5th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Sciences (AiDAS)
abstract: The expanding healthcare sector requires creative solutions to connect patients with vital information. Language barriers exacerbate the challenge, as many chatbots are predominantly English-based, limiting accessibility for non- English speakers. Therefore, this work introduces OYEN, a Large Language Model (LLM)-based chatbot designed for patients with bilingual (Mandarin and English) healthcare guidance. Early chatbot architectures relied on statistical Natural Language Processing (NLP) methods and keyword pattern recognition. However, the rise of LLMs with learning capabilities revolutionized chatbot development since 2018. Transformer-based LLMs became dominant due to their exceptional performance in modeling natural text. Developed for healthcare institutions in Malaysia offering Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) services, OYEN accurately responds to open-ended TCM-related questions. To ensure OYEN's capability to be user-language centric, responding in the language of the user's input (if a user inputs Mandarin, the response will be in Mandarin and vice versa for English language), a similarity search mechanism using a vector database which is known as Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) is integrated. This advanced technique enhances OYEN's ability to retrieve and present relevant TCM information.

titulo: Chunking for Medical Knowledge Dataset Construction and LLM-Based Question Answering
autores: Y. -J. Chiu; H. -Y. Chang; C. -C. Chuang
venue: 2025 15th International Conference on Biomedical Engineering and Technology (ICBET)
abstract: Large language models have demonstrated significant potential in medical applications, particularly in the construction of structured knowledge databases through retrieval-augmented generation systems. However, the optimization of chunking strategies in medical data processing remains an open challenge, as excessive segmentation may lead to retrieval inefficiencies while overly large chunks risk losing critical information. This study systematically evaluates the impact of chunking strategies on medical database construction, focusing on Traditional Chinese epilepsy guidelines. Using Llama 2-70b to generate structured question-answer datasets, we employ Gemini and Nemotron-4-340B-Instruct to assess data accuracy, consistency, and relevance through a reciprocal evaluation framework. Our findings reveal that while chunk size influences retrieval precision, inference length and response generation have a more significant impact on processing efficiency, with a strong correlation between inference length and generation time $(r= 0.89)$. Furthermore, the evaluation models exhibit notable differences: Gemini assigns higher and more consistent scores with faster processing times, while NVIDIA applies stricter evaluation criteria, resulting in lower scores and longer validation durations. These results highlight the importance of model selection in medical AI applications, as different LLMs prioritize different aspects of data quality. Additionally, the study suggests that optimizing inference structure and refining chunking methods are crucial for enhancing retrieval performance. Future research should explore advanced entity-linking techniques and cost-efficient deployment strategies to improve the scalability and reliability of RAG-based medical knowledge systems.

titulo: Enhancing RAG-Based Chatbots Through User Personalization and Knowledge Base Versioning within a Campus Environment
autores: M. A. Nugroho; E. M. Kusumaningtyas; A. R. Barakbah
venue: 2026 International Electronics Symposium (IES)
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) enhances Large Language Models (LLMs) with external knowledge, making it a highly promising technology for dynamic campus information systems. However, conventional RAG systems lack user personalization and document version control, often leading to generic responses and the risk of retrieving outdated academic regulations. To resolve these issues, this study proposes an enhanced RAG architecture that integrates user personalization and knowledge base versioning through persona metadata and semantic versioning (X.Y.Z) utilizing a hybrid SQL-vector search mechanism. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach successfully isolates context according to user roles (e.g., lecturers and students) and consistently retrieves the most accurate, up-to-date document versions while significantly optimizing search space and reducing system latency.

titulo: Enhancing College Student Mental Health Support using LLMs and RAG-Based Chatbot System: A Study Case in Institut Teknologi Bandung
autores: I. D. M. M. Pradnyana
venue: 2025 International Conference on ICT for Smart Society (ICISS)
abstract: Mental health issues are a critical concern among college students. Research has consistently demonstrated a significant negative correlation between symptoms such as stress, depression, and anxiety with students' academic achievement, ultimately undermining their educational attainment and long-term well-being. At Institut Teknologi Bandung (ITB), counseling services are available. However, several challenges persist, including limited appointment availability, waiting periods of one to two weeks when slots are fully booked, and the lack of other alternatives in providing quick and easily accessible initial support. This study explore a potential solution through the development and evaluation of a mental health chatbot system that combines Large Language Models (LLMs) with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). This study implemented two architectures: a standard RAG pipeline and an enhanced version using Hypothetical Document Embeddings (HyDE), testing both with closed-source (GPT-4.1-mini) and open-source (LLaMA-3.1-70b) models. The LLM-based evaluation indicates that HyDE generally enhances retrieval performance, although it may decrease when the hypothetical answers are irrelevant. The highest LLM-based evaluation score was achieved by configuration M-02 (gpt-4.1-mini with HyDE applied), with an overall average of 0.9182. The domain expert evaluation confirmed that the chatbot is reasonably capable of producing factual, coherent, comprehensive, and safe responses.

titulo: Greek-HemaRAG: A Retrieval-Augmented Generation System for Hematologic Malignancies in the Greek Language
autores: M. E. Chatzimina; M. Tsiknakis
venue: 2025 IEEE 25th International Conference on Bioinformatics and Bioengineering (BIBE)
abstract: Answering biomedical questions in Greek, especially in fields like hematologic malignancies, is still a significant challenge. This is mainly due to the lack of domainspecific corpora and tools for under-resourced languages. In this work, we present Greek-HemaRAG, a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system designed specifically for the Greek language and focused on blood cancers. The system brings together a dense retriever, enriched with biomedical ontologies, and a locally fine-tuned version of the Gemma 3 large language model. The training material included a combination of PubMed abstracts, filtered PubMedQA entries, and Greek biomedical texts from the CLARIN corpus. Biomedical enrichment using MeSH, NCIT, DOID, and UMLS synonyms was applied to improve coverage and retrieval precision. All components of the system run locally in order to ensure privacy and suitability in sensitive healthcare settings. Evaluation results on the translated BioASQ questions demonstrated high semantic similarity (BERTScore: 89%), strong recognition of medical terms (NER overlap: 74%1) and high retrieval performance (Recall@10: 95%). These results underscore the potential of Greek-HemaRAG to support accurate and privacyconscious medical question answering in low-resource languages like Greek.

titulo: Toward Inclusive Healthcare: An LLM-Based Multimodal Chatbot for Preliminary Diagnosis
autores: I. Agarwal; V. Sakthivel; P. Prakash
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: This paper presents the design and development of a multimodal medical chatbot that leverages Gemini-2.0-Flash Model alongside a novel Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture to support preliminary medical diagnosis and recommendations. The system integrates textual prompt analysis and medical image interpretation, aiming to improve healthcare accessibility, particularly for underserved populations. Focused on data-rich medical conditions, the chatbot generates reliable diagnostic insights based on natural language inputs and/or medical images, requiring minimal user expertise. The proposed RAG-based architecture incorporates a curated medical knowledge base and structured retrieval mechanisms, significantly reducing hallucinations and enhancing response credibility compared to direct Large Language Model (LLM) querying. By demonstrating the efficacy of multimodal reasoning in conjunction with structured retrieval, this work paves the way for more accessible, accurate, and scalable AI-driven health support systems.

titulo: PUENYAI Bot: A Retrieval-Augmented LLM Chatbot for University Information Services
autores: A. A. R. B. Ramli; W. Krathu; A. Bramantoro
venue: 2025 7th International Conference on Applied Computational Intelligence in Information Systems (ACIIS)
abstract: We present PUENYAI, a locally hosted retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) chatbot that answers enquiries on curricula, scholarships, and application procedures using institutional sources. Built entirely from open-source components and deployed on-premises, the system avoids external APIs while keeping answers grounded in official documents. This paper contributes three practical outcomes for higher-education deployments: (i) a reproducible on-prem blueprint—client, backend, embeddings, vector store, and locally served large language model (LLM)—together with the design trade-offs that led to these choices; (ii) a lightweight evaluation protocol (self-queries, structured user tests, and advisor review) that programs can reuse to check relevance, completeness, and policy alignment; and (iii) a set of lessons learned and governance guidelines (coverage of sources, chunking granularity, update workflow, and privacy controls) distilled from implementation. Results observed during formative testing indicate that a compact local stack consistently answers routine enquiries while reducing staff effort; remaining limitations (multilingual handling, admin tooling, and document structure) inform a practical roadmap for campus roll-outs.

titulo: MOPbot: A Harm-Reduction Chatbot for Opioid Overdose Prevention and Local Resource Navigation
autores: R. Cui; A. Kalaga; S. Velichety
venue: 2026 IEEE 14th International Conference on Healthcare Informatics (ICHI)
abstract: Opioid overdose remains a severe and preventable public health challenge, particularly for individuals with limited access to professional support and local resources. This work presents MOPbot, a grounded, harm-reduction-oriented chatbot designed to provide plain-language overdose education, connect users to local services, and support safer information access in a high-risk public health context. MOPbot combines a large language model with retrieval-augmented generation, planner-based tool routing, and a curated knowledge base containing resources, laws, statistics, and FAQs. The system also incorporates safety-aware design, including emergency detection and refusal of unsafe or illegal requests. A planned three-month pilot study will evaluate knowledge, resource awareness, help-seeking attitudes, usability, and engagement among approximately 50 participants recruited through Memphis nonprofits. These early findings and planned evaluations position MOPbot as a practical framework for community-specific overdose education and resource navigation.

titulo: RAGClin: A Privacy-Preserving Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework for Clinical Question
autores: B. N. Hiremath; S. Hiremath; N. R; N. J; N. V P; G. S. Tejas
venue: 2025 5th International Conference on Emerging Research in Electronics, Computer Science and Technology (ICERECT)
abstract: Generative AI is rapidly transforming healthcare by enabling smarter tools for clinical decision support, automated documentation, and patient interaction. However, alongside these opportunities, current Large Language Models (LLMs) present significant challenges: they frequently produce hallucinations—information that appears credible but is factually incorrect—and they often depend on cloud-based deployment, raising critical concerns about patient data privacy and compliance with healthcare regulations.As our key contribution, we present RAGClin, a privacy-preserving Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework designed for clinical question-answering. RAGClin combines synthetic medical documents with a local semantic search pipeline to supply verifiable context during inference. Using MiniLM for lightweight dense embeddings and a FAISS vector database for top-k cosine similarity retrieval, relevant context is dynamically fetched and appended to the user query. This combined input is processed by a locally hosted LLaMA 3.1 model via the Ollama runtime, ensuring that sensitive information remains fully local.By grounding generative outputs in domain-specific retrieved knowledge, our contribution mitigates hallucinations, improves factual accuracy, and upholds strict privacy requirements. Preliminary experiments show high semantic precision, reduced hallucination rates, and near real-time performance on both high-performance compute nodes and consumer-grade hardware. These results highlight RAGClin as a practical and secure approach for deploying trustworthy Generative AI in privacy-sensitive healthcare applications.

titulo: Multi-Agent RAG Chatbot: SIT Student Assistant
autores: N. Somroop; C. Limprasertsiri; P. Jirawatpapha; N. Waraporn; O. Rojanapornpun; N. Atiratana
venue: 2026 8th International Symposium on Computational and Business Intelligence (ISCBI)
abstract: Automated student assistants have become increasingly common in educational institutions, where students expect prompt and accurate responses from modern support systems. At the same time, large language models (LLMs), combined with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), have enabled human-like conversational interfaces over domain-specific vector databases. However, due to overlapping and imprecisely defined knowledge domains within organizations, conventional LLM-based RAG systems often struggle to deliver high-quality, domain-specific responses. To address this challenge, we propose a multi-agent RAG architecture that explicitly manages multiple knowledge domains and generates responses based on ranked retrieval scores. The proposed system was evaluated through deployment at our university, where experimental results demonstrate a high level of role adherence, effectively reducing hallucination and improving the reliability of the AI student assistant.

titulo: Indonesian Educational Chatbot for Sports, Health and Physical Education using Retrieval-Augmented Generation
autores: V. C. Mawardi; B. R. Trilaksono; A. Purwarianti
venue: 2025 International Conference on Data Science and Its Applications (ICoDSA)
abstract: This study evaluates the effect of retrieval embeddings and similarity metrics at the generative component (LLaMA3). No fine-tuning or decoding variation was applied to the generator, ensuring that any performance differences were due to retrieval quality alone. This design enables a focused evaluation of how retrieval configurations influence the final output in a controlled RAG setup, particularly for primary school topics in sports and health (PJOK). We point out that RAG is a technique that helps large language models make fewer mistakes by using outside information, which improves the accuracy of facts and the relevance of the context. The research compares various embedding models and retrieval similarity metrics to evaluate their effectiveness in retrieving relevant information. The baai/bge-m3 and gte-multilingual-base models demonstrate strong performance with 0.98 precision, while the indo-bge-m3 model shows high recall but lower precision. From 5 embeddings, Llama Embedding performs significantly worse than the other models. The dot product has higher recall than Euclidean and cosine similarity metrics but embedding model selection significantly influences overall performance. The study underscores the importance of embedding choice and retrieval quality in improving chatbot responses. Further refinements are suggested, including better filtering, reranking retrieved chunks, and fine-tuning the retriever, or LLaMA, to align with the target language domain, such as Bahasa Indonesia. The results show that even though RAG improves how well things are generated, the quality of what is retrieved is still a major problem, which means we need to keep making improvements for the best results in educational uses.

titulo: SymptoTrack-AI: A Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework for Intelligent Symptom Monitoring and Assessment
autores: L. A. S. Joysee; Z. M. Prakashitha
venue: 2026 8th International Conference on Inventive Material Science and Applications (ICIMA)
abstract: Fast and accurate symptom screening is a central need to proactive and convenient healthcare provision, especially in distant and resource-limited conditions. Current symptom checker applications and independent conversational agents have weaknesses of limited contextual accuracy, intermittent clinical accuracy, and hallucinating responses, limiting their usefulness in practice. In this paper, the suggested framework is SYMPTOTRACK-AI, a hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)-based conversational paradigm of intelligent symptom monitoring and initial clinical decision support. The suggested system combines systematic symptom value jointly, longitudinal patient context modeling, medical knowledge search through reputable sources and regulated generative reason to give clinically founded and risk-conscious answers. Triage and safety control module: Dedicated triage and safety control module will guarantee a conservative escalation of the high-risk cases, and self-care advice of the low-risk cases. Experimental testing proves that SYMPTOTRACK-AI is more diagnostic, has a significantly lower incidence of hallucinations, and better triage than rule-based, machine learning-based, and LLM-only symptom monitoring systems. The findings demonstrate the suitability of hybrid RAG structures to improve reliability, safety and user confidence on real-world digital healthcare services.

titulo: Ontology-Aware RAG for Improved Question-Answering in Cybersecurity Education
autores: C. Zhao; G. Agrawal; F. Zhang; T. Kumarage; Z. Tan; Y. Deng; Y. -C. Chen; H. Liu
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Big Data (BigData)
abstract: Integrating AI into education has the potential to transform the teaching of science and technology courses, particularly in the field of cybersecurity. AI-driven question-answering (QA) systems can actively manage uncertainty in cybersecurity problem-solving, offering interactive, inquiry-based learning experiences. Recently, Large language models (LLMs) have gained prominence in AI-driven QA systems, enabling advanced language understanding and user engagement. However, they face challenges like hallucinations and limited domain-specific knowledge, which reduce their reliability in educational settings. To address these challenges, we propose CyberRAG, an ontology-aware retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) approach for developing a reliable and safe QA system in cybersecurity education. Cyberrag employs a two-step approach: first, it augments the domain-specific knowledge by retrieving validated cybersecurity documents from a knowledge base to enhance the relevance and accuracy of the response. Second, it mitigates hallucinations and misuse by integrating a knowledge graph ontology to validate the final answer. Comprehensive experiments on publicly available datasets reveal that CyberRAG delivers accurate, reliable responses aligned with domain knowledge, demonstrating the potential of AI tools to enhance education.

titulo: MedRAGShield: A Three-Tier Defense Framework Against Document Poisoning and Adversarial Attacks in Medical Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
autores: M. Shanid; G. Prasad; V. Bawgi; S. Gowda
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Emerging Synergy Science and Technology (ICESST)
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems deployed in medical question-answering applications introduce novel attack surfaces not addressed by existing large language model (LLM) safety mechanisms. This research presents MedRAGShield, a three-tier middleware defense framework designed to detect and neutralise document injection poisoning, hallucination exploitation, prompt injection, and jailbreak attacks against medical RAG pipelines. The proposed system operates across three independently togglable defense modes: a baseline mode with no filtering, a confidence and hallucination gating mode, and a full defense mode augmenting the prior modes with Domain-Aware Sanity Check (DASC) rules that apply medical ontological constraints to generated outputs. This experiment constructs a 40-query adversarial evaluation dataset spanning four attack categories and conducts an empirical evaluation on a clinical pharmacology RAG system built on Llama 3.2:3B and ChromaDB.
