Our contribution is an end-to-end methodology for building a domain-specific chatbot, including the curation of a knowledge base from over 20,000 PubMed Central articles. The system incorporates a Query Transformation step, where an LLM reformulates user questions into technical biomedical search phrases to improve retrieval accuracy. PhysioRAG links all generated statements to their corresponding PubMed sources, further enforcing citation-grounded responses. This work details the system architecture and evaluation, demonstrating a robust and transparent solution for trustworthy medical information delivery.

titulo: Post-hoc Verification of LLMs with Knowledge Graphs for Medical Question Answering
autores: I. Boutra; H. Slimi; M. Y. Haouam; I. Bendib
venue: 2025 International Conference on Recent Advances in Mathematics and Informatics (ICRAMI)
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable progress in natural language processing and show strong potential for medical question answering (QA). Their ability to process biomedical literature and generate coherent responses makes them attractive for clinical and research applications. However, their deployment in high-stakes domains is limited due to critical issues such as hallucinations, outdated knowledge, and lack of verifiability. These shortcomings undermine reliability and highlight the need for mechanisms that can ensure factual grounding. We propose a lightweight post-hoc verification framework that integrates LLMs with biomedical Knowledge Graphs (KGs). Using the Gene Ontology (GO) as a domain-specific resource, our framework extracts factual statements from LLM-generated responses, reformulates them as KG queries, and validates them against curated biomedical knowledge. Unsupported claims are flagged or corrected through an optional refinement loop, improving factual consistency without requiring retraining or fine-tuning of the base LLM. We evaluate the framework on two datasets with different characteristics: PubMedQA, a benchmark of general biomedical questions derived from PubMed abstracts, and GO-QA, a domain-specific dataset constructed from Gene Ontology concepts. Results show consistent improvements in factual accuracy, with BERT-F1 increasing from 0.4110 to 0.4245 on PubMedQA and from 0.8242 to 0.8405 on GO-QA. These findings demonstrate that posthoc KG verification is a practical and generalizable strategy for enhancing the reliability and trustworthiness of LLM-based medical QA systems.

titulo: E-GPT: A Multi-Agent LLM Framework for Intelligent Educational Assistance
autores: T. Ara; S. Panda; J. S. Das; A. R. Das; S. V. Prabhugoankar
venue: 2025 1st International Conference on Advancement in Futuristic Technologies (ICAFT)
abstract: Recent developments in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Natural Language Processing (NLP) have significantly influenced the education sector, mainly through Large Language Models (LLMs) and Multi-Agent Systems (MAS). Educational chatbots such as GPTutor use Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and transformer-based models to offer more intelligent tutoring and automated assessment support. Still, most existing systems depend on centralized APIs and monolithic designs, which restrict scalability, adaptability to different contexts, and data privacy.In this paper, we introduce E-GPT, a locally deployable multi-agent educational chatbot framework designed to divide learning tasks among independent, specialized agents. These include a PDF-to-Quiz Generator, PDF-to-Technical Article Writer, RAG-based Chat Assistant, Question Paper Generator, and an OCR-enabled PDF Analyzer. The system integrates fine-tuned versions of LLaMA3 and Mistral models with a MongoDB-FAISS vector database, allowing efficient context retrieval and smooth collaboration between agents.Experimental results show that E-GPT improves contextual accuracy, modular scalability, and response time while maintaining user data privacy. By distributing different cognitive functions across coordinated agents, the system takes a step toward building a more adaptive, transparent, and scalable AI-driven learning environment.

titulo: Generative AI-Driven Digital Health Expert Twin
autores: A. Chougale; R. Dashrath; R. Badarkhe; D. A. Chavan
venue: 2026 2nd International Conference on Information, Implementation and Innovation in Technology (I2ITCON)
abstract: The multimodal generative AI is revolutionizing patient guidance by moving away from static symptom checkers towards intelligent, context-aware healthcare ecosystems. The paper proposes a high-performance Generative AI-Driven Health Expert Twin that is intended for real-time clinical assistance. The proposed system is distinguished from existing text-based chatbots by its combination of large language models (LLMs) and retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) that is grounded on a massive 6-volume medical knowledge base: The Gale Encyclopedia of Medicine. The proposed system utilizes GROQ’s high-speed LLM inference models within a local environment to attain high-speed response time requirements for seamless voice, image, and text interactions. The proposed system is distinguished by its two-storage approach to medical knowledge retrieval using FAISS and patient memory preservation using SQLite. The proposed system is further distinguished by its Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS), which checks for drug interactions, generates emergency pop-up alerts for "Red Flag" symptoms, and generates telemedicine suggestions. The proposed system has been experimentally proven to attain significant improvements in diagnostic grounding and safety layer reliability, thereby offering a robust roadmap for scalability and privacy-aware digital health twins.

titulo: CRITIC-RAG: Knowledge-Augmented Large Language Models With Verified Retrieval for Improved Medical Reasoning
autores: J. Li; L. Lu; Y. Miao; Y. Tian; J. Li
venue: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
abstract: While retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) presents a promising solution for enhancing large language models (LLMs) in question answering (QA), particularly in knowledge-intensive domains like medicine, it continues to face challenges related to factual consistency and reasoning reliability. To address this challenge, we propose CRITIC-RAG, a verification-enhanced framework that integrates a small-size, instruction-tuned verifier throughout the RAG pipeline. Our method incorporates selective retrieval, evidence filtering, structured reasoning through self-consistency, and groundedness verification. This approach enhances the accurate utilization of external knowledge while reducing spurious generations. Comprehensive experiments across five medical QA benchmarks and multiple LLM backbones confirm the framework's broad applicability and plug-and-play adaptability. For instance, CRITIC-RAG improves accuracy from 41.3% to 48.8% on MedQA and boosts BERTScore from 68.1% to 74.4% on MedicationQA using LLaMA-3. Ablation studies further reveal that evidence filtering and structured reasoning are especially critical to robust performance. Case studies and retrieval analyses, including improvements in entailment-based similarity scores and factual accuracy, demonstrate how each stage of verification jointly contributes to generating more accurate, evidence-grounded responses. Overall, our work highlights verification as a key mechanism for enhancing trustworthiness in knowledge-intensive medical QA, a capability that is increasingly important for clinical decision support and other real-world healthcare applications.

titulo: Chimera-3X: A Hybrid Cognitive Engine for Retrieval-Augmented Biomedical Consulting
autores: M. Dhifallah; Y. Liu
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Bioinformatics and Biomedicine (BIBM)
abstract: Biomedical question answering remains a challenging task due to the complexity of clinical knowledge and the limitations of general-purpose large language models (LLMs) in providing accurate, domain-specific responses. We introduce Chimera-3X, a hybrid cognitive engine that orchestrates multiple specialized LLMs (DeepSeek, BioGPT from Microsoft, and Exone 3.0 from LG), each fine-tuned and adapted as an independent medical sub-toolkit. Chimera-3X integrates external biomedical knowledge graphs such as UMLS, SNOMED CT, and Wikidata via retrieval-augmented generation techniques, enhancing the system's factual accuracy and reasoning capabilities. Each engine processes clinical queries independently while the orchestrator coordinates their outputs, leveraging SPARQLbased queries to ensure precise knowledge retrieval. Preliminary evaluations demonstrate significant improvements in clinical answer accuracy, coherence, and interpretability compared to standalone LLM approaches. We propose an architecture that provides a scalable, transparent and effective framework for biomedical consulting, advancing the integration of knowledgedriven AI in healthcare applications. Code and Resources: https://github.com/marwan8086/Chimera-3X

titulo: Retrieval Augmented MedLM
autores: S. Devi; G. Dhar; C. Bharadwaj; A. M
venue: 2024 IEEE Conference on Artificial Intelligence (CAI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to leverage large language models (LLMs) for medical question answering (QA) by integrating them with external knowledge sources. We utilize de-identified clinical discharge notes from MIMIC-IV and Apollo Hospitals as our data source. We propose a novel summarization technique that extracts and condenses the core medical information from the discharge notes, eliminating unnecessary verbosity. This results in concise "medical summaries" that effectively inform the LLM while reducing context overload. We evaluate our approach using RAGAS, a novel framework for label-free evaluation of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines. Clinician validation further confirms the effectiveness of our approach, highlighting its potential to enhance medical QA systems.

titulo: RAG for Question-Answering for Vocal Training Based on Domain Knowledge Base
autores: C. -h. J. Leung; Y. Yi; L. Kuai; Z. Li; S. -k. A. Yeung; K. -w. J. Lee; K. -h. K. Ho; K. Hung
venue: 2024 11th International Conference on Behavioural and Social Computing (BESC)
abstract: Although Large language models (LLMs) are well-known due to their superior capacity for text generation and logical inference, they are found to be inaccurate in domain-specific question-answering tasks. The powerful generator still tends to generate content even when the LLM does not have sufficient knowledge at all, which is known as the hallucination problem. We find there is a research void in applying LLMs in the vocal training industry, which requires intensive expert knowledge in any chatbot or intelligent tutor services. This paper details employing Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) technology to develop a domain-specific language model, addressing inherent challenges such as hallucination, where large models generate plausible but inaccurate content, and lack of domain specificity. By segmenting the knowledge base and establishing semantic similarities between user queries and knowledge data, the project lays a solid foundation for integrating RAG, significantly improving response accuracy and contextual relevance. The report highlights the successful implementation of RAG, enhancing system intelligence and personalization for user-specific needs, discusses challenges and solutions during the implementation process, and outlines future directions to expand RAG capabilities and improve user experiences.

titulo: Multi-Agent Medical Debate System for Clinical Reasoning
autores: S. Bhoyar; A. Ansari; N. Saxena
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Industry 4.0, Artificial Intelligence, and Communications Technology (IAICT)
abstract: Clinical deployment of large language models (LLMs) for medical question answering faces three primary challenges: (1) models frequently produce unsupported or hallucinated claims because their parametric knowledge is not verified against biomedical evidence; (2) single-pass inference prevents iterative self-correction, leading to incomplete differential diagnoses; and (3) poorly calibrated confidence scores undermine clinician trust. To address these challenges, we introduce a retrieval augmented multi-agent model whose components are specifically designed to generate medical answers through three stages: hypothesis generation, adversarial debate, and independent judgment, wherein evidence conditioned hypotheses are generated, contested by an adversarial process, and finally evaluated by an independent model. Each of these models utilizes a semantic retrieval system to access medical literature from PubMed, explanations of answer benchmarks from MedQA, and medical records from MIMIC III. The model is evaluated using the MedQA USMLE benchmark and a collection of prompts created from MIMIC III data, as well as by comparing the performance of the system against a general purpose LLM and a fine tuned medical LLM. Results indicate that the approach described improves the supported sentences rate, the precision and recall of the attributed sentences, and the groundedness of the answers provided while also reducing the number of unsupported claims, hallucinations, Brier score, and expected calibration error, while maintaining the same accuracy in medical diagnosis. Thus, these findings indicate that the incorporation of adversarial and verification models during inference can improve the model’s ability to align with the evidence and to calibrate uncertainty in its predictions without requiring any adaptation to the models with supervised training data.

titulo: SmartEduNotes: A Retrieval-Augmented Platform for Personalized Note-Taking, Revision, and Career Guidance
autores: V. Singh; T. K. Pradhan; S. SS; K. Upadhayay; S. S. Kumar
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Interdisciplinary Approaches in Technology and Management for Social Innovation (IATMSI)
abstract: Effective learning in modern education requires tools that not only store information but actively help learners retain knowledge and plan future careers. We present SmartEduNotes, a web-based, retrieval-augmented platform that enhances personal note-taking through dense semantic search, provenance-aware question answering, automated flashcard generation, and concept-graph-driven career guidance. The system integrates Sentence-BERT embeddings, FAISS vector search, and LLM-based generation to provide accurate, context-grounded answers from personal notes, while automatically converting content into cloze-style flashcards scheduled with our novel Adaptive SM-2 algorithm for optimized spaced repetition. Central concepts extracted via a concept graph inform personalized skill recommendations based on real-world job postings. Pilot evaluation on 150 lecture note documents demonstrates up to 87 % QA accuracy, 85% 7-day flashcard recall (compared to 62 % manually), and effective identification of career-relevant skills. The architecture supports modular expansion, multi-modal input (audio, text), on-device privacy, and adaptive learning strategies. This work contributes a reproducible framework for personalized learning, knowledge retention, and career-aligned skill development.

titulo: RAG-Enhanced Healthcare Integration LLM Framework
autores: O. Dawood; W. Ismaiel; Y. Elhakeem; H. Nayel
venue: 2026 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Systems, and Emerging Technologies (ICAISET)
abstract: With the revolution of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated great capabilities in healthcare transformation through clinical question answering, medical decision support, and patient communication. However, the deployment of LLMs in real-world healthcare environments faces many challenges such as hallucination, lack of transparency, data privacy, and insufficient accountability. The paper proposes to use Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and developed a theoretical RAG-Enhanced healthcare LLM framework to address these limitations through component integration architecture. The proposed framework integrates contextual retrieval, confidence aware scoring, provenance tagging, and clinical guardrails with mandatory human-in-the-loop oversight. The framework reduces the risks of hallucination and other limitations of LLMs. The empirical assessment of the framework’s impact on diagnostic accuracy, clinical decision-making, and patient outcomes is the future work of this study.

titulo: The Impact of Ontology Structure in the Performance of RAG Systems: a Medical Use Case
autores: D. Lin; A. Riquelme-García; J. T. Fernández-Breis; P. E. Anderson
venue: 2026 IEEE Conference on Artificial Intelligence (CAI)
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a widely used framework for circumventing the knowledge constraints of LLMs. General-purpose RAG systems are naive to domain-specific terminology and structure. As a result, prior work such as OG-RAG leverages ontologies to bake expert knowledge and domain understanding into RAG systems. However, the feasibility, effectiveness, and accuracy of OG-RAG is completely dependent on the ontology. In order to build new ontologies and modify existing ontologies for OG-RAG, it is critical to understand how structural aspects of an ontology impact performance. In this study, we systematically evaluate how the structure of an ontology determines performance across two key tasks: document-to-ontology mapping, and question-answering. To measure its performance, we applied OG-RAG across two specialized domains: chronic lower back pain and spinal cord injury rehabilitation. We measured how the specificity of the ontology classes can impact the performance of OG-RAG, finding that an ontology containing more general classes can reduce the risk of hallucinations during document-to-ontology mapping, while using specific instance-level classes can hinder accuracy. Furthermore, we investigate the impact of adding class descriptions on OG-RAG behavior, revealing an increase in performance when providing the additional context. Our results identify potential best practices when building ontologies for OG-RAG, enabling its application across domains.

titulo: Emotion-Aware Digital Therapy Assistant Using LLMs and Agentic Workflows
autores: P. Patel; K. Kumar; H. Verma; H. R. Chaubey; R. Kandari
venue: 2026 IEEE 1st International Conference on Intelligent Technologies for a Sustainable and Inclusive Future (ICITSIF)
abstract: Digital mental-health systems are increasingly deployed as first-line support for stress, anxiety, and mood disorders, yet many conversational agents still lack reliable emotionawareness, safety mechanisms, and clinically grounded escalation paths. This paper presents an Emotion-Aware Digital Therapy Assistant that combines large language models (LLMs), multimodal emotion detection, and agentic workflows to deliver context-sensitive and safety-conscious mental-wellness support. The assistant first estimates the user’s affective state from text and conversational context, then evaluates psychological risk using a healthcare-tuned LLM and rule-based safety graph, and finally chooses between therapeutic conversation, coping exercises, or escalation to emergency workflows (e.g., crisis alerts, human clinicians). We design a realistic benchmark—EMOThera—comprising 8,500 annotated utterances across seven emotion categories and three risk levels and report results on emotion classification, crisis detection, latency, and user experience. The proposed system achieves 89.7% macro accuracy and 0.88 macro F1 for emotion recognition, 0.91 AUC for high-risk detection, and a median end-to-end latency of 430ms per turn on commodity hardware, while 81.3% of participants in a small pilot (n = 32) report feeling "emotionally understood". These findings suggest that combining LLMs with structured safety workflows and lightweight multimodal modeling can yield an accessible, low-friction, and safer pathway between self-help tools and professional mental-health care.

titulo: NexaLearn: A Generative AI-Based Multimodal Framework for Interactive Video Learning Assistance
autores: H. Srivastava; D. Srivastava; J. Agrahari; A. P. Singh; A. Singh
venue: 2026 IEEE Madhya Pradesh Section Conference (MPCON)
abstract: The meteoric increase in popularity of video-based e-learning platforms has made learning more accessible; nevertheless, due chiefly to their passive nature, these platforms fail to foster interactivity between learners themselves, actual contextualization of information, and retention. In this paper, we present a multimodal generative AI learning assistant based on interactivity and personalized learning from videos. The working framework comprises automatic speech recognition for extracting transcripts aligned with video over time, transformer models for embedding-based semantic representation, and FAISS-based retrieval from an indexed corpus of dense vector representations supporting retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). Multimodal content understanding gets realized by the application of optical character recognition and computer vision for extracting textual and visual information from lecture slides and diagrams. An interactive chatbot built using a large language model provides context-aware question answering using retrieved video segments tied to the exact timestamps. The system was built on scalable web architecture, with React.js as a front-end technology, Python Flask/FastAPI service as a back end for processing, and a cloud-hosted vector database for efficient indexing and retrieval. Experimental evaluation based on retrieval relevance and response accuracy metrics proves reduced information access time and increased learning efficiency. The proposed system converts the passive consumption of videos into an active intelligent and learner-centered educational experience.

titulo: A Unified Framework for AR Indoor Navigation and Conversational Information Retrieval in Smart Campus Environments
autores: A. Magdy; A. Mohamed; A. A. Boghdady; B. Achraf; H. Mohamed; Z. Abd-El-Hamid; S. Ali; I. Hegazy
venue: 2025 Twelfth International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Information Systems (ICICIS)
abstract: Navigating complex indoor environments like university campuses poses a significant challenge, compounded by the difficulty of accessing specific institutional information. While vision-based Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) offers continuous tracking, it suffers from cumulative drift. Sim- ilarly, standard Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems for question-answering are prone to context collision. This paper presents a unified mobile application that integrates a robust AR indoor navigation module with an intelligent conversational assistant to address both challenges simultaneously. The pro- posed navigation system fuses the continuous motion tracking of SLAM with high-precision QR code markers for drift correction, providing accurate, real-time visual guidance. For information retrieval, a novel RAG architecture is proposed featuring an LLM-powered router that intelligently directs user queries to one of several specialized vector stores, effectively eliminating con- text collision and improving contextual accuracy. Experimental results confirm that the navigation module provides robust and accurate visual guidance in real-world scenarios. Furthermore, the chatbot's router-based architecture demonstrates a marked improvement in retrieval accuracy, consistently identifying more relevant information than a standard RAG system. The proposed system demonstrates the feasibility of synergistically combining spatial computing with advanced conversational AI to create a comprehensive smart campus assistant, enhancing the student experience by providing seamless access to both physical and digital resources.

titulo: Enhancing Intelligent Tutoring Systems with Large Language Models: Architecture and Implementation
autores: R. Abaab; M. A. Khenissi
venue: 2025 10th International Conference on ICT & Accessibility (ICTA) co-located with 2025 2nd International Conference and Forum on Assistive Technologies for Special Needs (ATSN)
abstract: Intelligent Tutoring Systems (ITSs) have proven effective in delivering adaptive and personalized instruction, yet their scalability remains limited by the high cost of authoring and maintaining instructional content. Recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) offer new opportunities to enrich ITSs with natural dialogue, dynamic explanations, and personalized feedback. However, challenges such as factual accuracy, reliability, and pedagogical alignment hinder their direct use in education. This paper presents a case study and technical implementation of a successful integration of LLMs within an ITS framework. The proposed architecture combines a recommendation engine with an LLM-powered chatbot, supported by grounding, scaffolding, and verification mechanisms to ensure pedagogical soundness. In this paper, we describe the layered system design, core integration components, and interaction pipeline that enable seamless learner engagement. Our contribution demonstrates how LLMs can complement ITSs in practice, reducing authoring effort, improving adaptability, and enhancing learner interaction through a reliable hybrid approach.

titulo: AI-Powered Framework for developing Virtual labs in Higher Education
autores: M. J. Almasri; A. S. Imran; A. Mavroudi; A. Soylu
venue: 2026 IEEE Global Engineering Education Conference (EDUCON)
abstract: The digitization of higher education has intensified the need for scalable, pedagogically grounded solutions to deliver hands-on, lab-based learning in online environments. This paper presents a five-layer framework for designing AI-powered virtual labs with authoring tools that integrate constructivism, Bloom’s Taxonomy, the Watch-Try-Do instructional model, AI-driven tutoring via LLM/RAG, xAPI-enabled learning analytics, and scalability and data ethics into a coherent implementation roadmap. The framework is instantiated through an Excel lesson on formulas that operationalizes all layers using a Watch-Try-Do sequence, an embedded GPT-4o-mini chatbot, and xAPI tracking to a Learning Record Store. A formative mixed-methods evaluation with ten staff at the University College of Applied Sciences in Gaza examined implementation outcomes (Acceptability, Appropriateness, Feasibility, Concerns) and adoption conditions. Reliability was satisfactory to excellent across constructs, and descriptive statistics with one-sample Wilcoxon tests showed Appropriateness and Feasibility to be above a neutral benchmark, while Acceptability was positive but sensitive to conservative inference and Concerns were heterogeneous rather than uniformly high. Thematic analysis of open-ended responses surfaced key benefits, barriers, enablers, and needs for institutional adoption. Triangulated mixed-method findings position the framework as pilot-ready under phased implementation and identify critical enabling conditions required to sustainably scale AI-powered Vlabs in higher education. The study contributes to a transferable model, an instantiated use case, and initial empirical evidence to guide the design and rollout of AI-powered virtual labs in higher education.

titulo: ThriveBuddy: Towards Student Well-being Through AI-Powered Digital Mentorship
autores: S. Palahan
venue: 2024 17th International Congress on Advanced Applied Informatics (IIAI-AAI-Winter)
abstract: This paper presents ThriveBuddy, a work-in-progress Q&A system and LLM-based chatbot designed to enhance student well-being and academic success by offering research-backed, practical advice for life improvement. The system uses interviews from credible YouTube sources as its external data corpus, providing students with evidence-based tips on topics such as stress management, productivity, and personal development. Initial evaluations highlight the effectiveness of MiniLM as the retrieval model, achieving the highest precision (0.2515), recall (0.7544), and F1-score (0.3772) for accurate document retrieval. For response generation, BART emerged as the optimal model, delivering the highest Answer Correctness (0.5255) along with strong scores in Answer Relevancy (0.7792) and Faithfulness (0.4080). These results underscore ThriveBuddy's potential as an accessible, supportive tool for students, with further refinements planned through a pilot study at a university in Thailand to enhance its accuracy, usability, and impact.

titulo: Ethical Prompt Optimization for Mental Health Chatbots Using Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) and Guardrail LLMs
autores: S. C. VR; G. Senthilvel P
venue: 2026 International Conference on Innovations in Communication, Geoscience and Robotics (ICICGR)
abstract: Large language model-powered mental health chatbots can improve mental health assistance, but they pose ethical hazards such crisis management, misleading empathy, and harmful discrimination. Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures and guardrail big language models are used to optimise mental health counselling prompts while ensuring ethical alignment. Domain specialists in crisis management, coping methods, psychoeducation, and empathetic reactions are combined with reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) under ethical limitations. Moderated input, expert routing, guardrail validation, and output screening are performed via a multi-layer safety pipeline. A publicly available mental health counselling dataset shows 94.3% safety compliance, 87.2% contextual adaptability, and 91.5% crisis detection sensitivity with 42% lower computing cost than dense baselines. Ethics-by-design improves safety without compromising therapeutic quality by bridging the gap between ethical AI concepts and susceptible domain implementation.

titulo: Agentic AI for Therapy
autores: S. Yadav; A. K. Sam; J. Jitto; J. V. L
venue: 2026 9th International Conference on Computational Intelligence in Data Science (ICCIDS)
abstract: Existing Large Language Model (LLM) based systems for mental health support are often unsafe and unreliable, primarily due to the absence of dynamic, user-controlled memory. This limitation leads to inconsistent therapeutic continuity and undermines the user trust necessary for forming meaningful therapeutic alliances. This paper introduces an Agentic Therapeutic Agent designed to address these challenges through a modular architecture that prioritizes safety, transparency, and long-term relationship building. The proposed framework's core feature is a secure Long-Term Memory system with a user-facing control panel and pathways for human therapist oversight. Initial development has produced two foundational, non-integrated modules: a rudimentary conversational AI and an effective crisis detection model intended to function as the first component of the agent's Safety & Guardrail Layer. The central contribution of this project is the design, implementation, and validation of this transparent memory architecture, which will integrate the conversational and safety modules. This approach directly addresses the critical gaps of memory and trust in therapeutic AI, demonstrating a tangible pathway toward a more ethically guided and effective support tool.

titulo: Proactive Mental Health Assistance via Agentic LLM Chatbots with Retrieval-Augmented Generation
autores: Wajiha, Shaira; Ghosh, Robin
venue: J. Comput. Sci. Coll.
abstract: Mental health challenges such as anxiety and depression are widespread, yet often remain unaddressed due to stigma, financial barriers, limited access to professionals, or personal reluctance. To address this gap, we present an accessible AI-powered chatbot that provides preliminary conversational support with empathetic, context-aware responses. The chatbot is trained and evaluated on two publicly available counseling conversation datasets from Huggingface, enabling it to learn and maintain therapeutic dialogue patterns. We compare three advanced LLMs, such as Llama3.1, Mistral 7b, and Qwen3, evaluating them on relevance, empathy, conciseness, and contextual understanding, and all models demonstrate high response quality. Incorporation of a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline with Facebook AI Similarity Search (FAISS) enhances factual accuracy and contextual relevance while reducing hallucinations. A key innovation is the integration of agentic AI, empowering the chatbot to recognize extreme distress and, with user consent, assist in scheduling appointments with mental health professionals. Overall, our system demonstrates the potential to deliver reliable, empathetic, and actionable conversational AI support for individuals experiencing early-stage mental health distress.

titulo: From Retrieval to Generation: Unifying External and Parametric Knowledge for Medical Question Answering
autores: Li, Lei; Zhou, Xiao; Zhang, Yingying; Wu, Xian
venue: Proceedings of the ACM Web Conference 2026
abstract: Medical question answering (QA) demands reliable access to rich, domain-specific knowledge. A prevalent strategy enhances large language models (LLMs) with either external knowledge retrieved from medical corpora or parametric knowledge embedded with model parameters. Existing methods generally fall into two paradigms: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), which grounds reasoning in retrieved evidence, and Generation-Augmented Generation (GAG), which relies exclusively on internally generated contexts. However, RAG often suffers from noisy or incomplete retrieval, whereas GAG is prone to hallucinated or inaccurate content due to unconstrained generation. Both limitations can misguide reasoning and compromise answer reliability. To overcome these challenges, we propose MedRGAG, a unified retrieval--generation augmented framework that seamlessly integrates external and parametric knowledge for medical QA. MedRGAG consists of two core modules: Knowledge-Guided Context Completion (KGCC), which steers the generator to produce background documents that complement knowledge gaps revealed by retrieval, and Knowledge-Aware Document Selection (KADS), which adaptively selects an optimal combination of retrieved and generated documents to construct concise yet comprehensive evidence for answers. Extensive experiments on five medical QA benchmarks demonstrate that MedRGAG achieves a 12.5\% improvement over MedRAG and a 4.5\% gain over MedGENIE, highlighting the effectiveness of unifying retrieval and generation for knowledge-intensive medical reasoning. Further analyses show that our framework effectively generates complementary contexts and recovers informative retrieved evidence. Our code and data are publicly available at https://github.com/ll0ruc/MedRGAG.

titulo: LLM-based Enhanced Question Answering System in Medical Domain
autores: Ganar, Rashmi; Dharme, Om A; Gharat, Smit A; Yadav, Anushka A; Parab, Arya A; Radke, Mansi A
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 8th Artificial Intelligence and Cloud Computing Conference
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) represent a major advancement in the field of natural language processing, capable of understanding, generating and interacting with human language at a near-human level. LLMs show strong potential in medical QA, information retrieval and predictive analysis. In contrast to general applications, mistakes in medical settings can have severe implications, making it crucial often struggle with hallucinations, misinterpretations, or outdated knowledge, which limits their reliability in high-stakes medical environments. This paper addresses the research gap by exploring techniques to enhance the reliability and performance of LLMs in biomedical applications, evaluating BioMedGPT, BioMedicine and BioMistral on PubMedQA and BioASQ datasets. To mitigate hallucinations and improve reliability, we applied a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) approach, achieving modest improvements. To overcome RAG’s limitations, we further explored a Graph RAG method using the Hetionet knowledge graph for better factual grounding. The results of this paper show promising results to advance the state of art in the biomedical domain. By using techniques like RAG and Graph RAG, we have addressed challenges related to accuracy and contextual relevance. With continued refinement, these models hold significant potential to enhance healthcare applications offering reliable, dependable and precise support for both clinicians and patients.

titulo: Balancing Health Information-Seeking through Retrieval-Augmented Generation-Based LLM Chatbot
autores: Nandy, Gargi; Gupta, Srishti; Mohammad Afzali, Farhad; Peeples, Eric; Pilon, Betsy; Tsai, Chun-Hua
venue: Adjunct Proceedings of the 33rd ACM Conference on User Modeling, Adaptation and Personalization
abstract: Family caregivers play a vital role in supporting children with chronic health conditions, such as neonates diagnosed with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE). However, navigating complex medical information can be overwhelming due to the quantity and quality of available literature. This study leverages Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)-based Large Language Models (LLMs) to develop a chatbot that integrates peer-reviewed scientific literature and provides personalized, simplified summaries for caregivers. A user study involving six caregivers and five healthcare providers demonstrated the chatbot’s ability to enhance clarity, improve comprehension, and deliver essential medical information concisely. Our findings highlight the potential of RAG-based LLMs to enhance caregivers’ health literacy and support their information-seeking behavior, while also underscoring the importance of thoughtfully navigating the differing expectations of caregivers and healthcare providers regarding the type, depth, and presentation of medical information.

titulo: GraphRAG-TCM: A Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation System for Traditional Chinese Medicine Clinical Decision Support
autores: Wang, Xian-Fang; Ren, Hao; Wang, Xiao-Lei; Han, Zi-Rui; Qin, Pei-Wu
venue: Proceedings of the 2026 2nd International Symposium on Bioinformatics and Computational Biology
abstract: Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) relies on intricate knowledge systems encompassing syndromes, herbs, formulas, and symptoms. Large Language Models (LLMs) show potential in medical question answering but often produce inaccurate information and struggle with domain-specific reasoning. This paper introduces GraphRAG-TCM, a combined Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) approach merging dense vector retrieval and knowledge graph exploration. We built a TCM knowledge graph with 112,751 nodes and 95,619 relationships across seven entity categories: Disease, Formula, Herb, Ingredient, Symptom, Syndrome, and Target. Our hybrid retrieval combines FAISS, BM25, and Neo4j graph traversal via Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF), with dictionary-based entity recognition and rule-based intent classification. We assess the system using Key-Fact F1 and Hallucination Rate (HR) metrics, avoiding biases from LLM-based judging. On 50 annotated TCM test cases, our system attains a Key-Fact F1 of 0.835 and a hallucination rate of 0.15\%, surpassing both pure LLM and standard RAG baselines.

titulo: Towards Reliable Medical Question Answering: A GraphRAG Framework with Deep Semantic Reasoning and Evidence Provenance
autores: Liu, Xuanwen
venue: Proceedings of the 2nd International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Applications
abstract: Clinical deployment of Large Language Models (LLMs) is severely bottle-necked by factual hallucinations, while traditional Knowledge Graph Question Answering (KGQA) architectures are constrained by rigid templates and limited multi-hop reasoning. To resolve this, we formulate a novel Graph-enhanced Retrieval-Augmented Generation (GraphRAG) framework for reliable, interpretable medical QA. Methodologically, we construct a massive medical knowledge graph via Open Information Extraction (OpenIE) and integrate Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to encode topological structures, enabling complex latent reasoning. The retrieved subgraphs subsequently act as factual anchors to augment the LLM, systematically mitigating hallucination risks. Coupled with an evidence provenance mechanism for verifiability, our framework empirically outperforms baseline LLMs and KGQA systems across accuracy, reasoning depth, and factual fidelity.

titulo: Study of Intelligent Question Answering System for the Course of Operating System
autores: Qin, Haiou; Chen, Huiyi; Huang, Jiajun; Xu, Lihuang; Li, Xianhe; Qiu, Zikun
venue: Proceedings of the 2026 International Conference on Big Data and Informatization Education
abstract: With the rapid development of computer technology and large models, traditional teaching methods and question-and-answer formats are unable to meet people's growing demand for quick access to accurate information in specific field. An intelligent question-and-answer platform for operating systems presented in this paper is based on retrieval augmented generation (RAG) and large language models (LLMs), adopting a multi-level retrieval enhancement strategy, introducing optical character recognition (OCR) to achieve multi-modal capabilities.

titulo: (wt) GC-DPG: Graph-Constrained Dual-Phase Generation for Safe and Verifiable Chinese Medical Question Answering
autores: Xie, Haihua; He, Miao
venue: Companion Proceedings of the ACM Web Conference 2026
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown strong performance on open-domain question answering, but their tendency to hallucinate unverifiable or unsafe medical content limits their applicability in clinical decision support and patient education. In contrast, high-quality medical knowledge graphs (KGs) encode curated relations between diseases, symptoms, drugs, examinations, and diet. We propose GC-DPG (Graph-Constrained Dual-Phase Generation), a two-phase framework that tightly couples an LLM with a disease-centric KG for Chinese medical QA. In the first phase, GC-DPG performs graph-based answer planning : given a user question and a disease KG, it constructs a structured, disease-specific Answer Plan that enumerates which KG facts are permissible for each detected intent (e.g., symptoms, checks, drugs). In the second phase, GC-DPG performs graph-constrained generation and consistency checking : it converts the Answer Plan into a constrained prompt that explicitly restricts the LLM to the planned entities, then applies a bidirectional graph--answer consistency checker to compute a support ratio and detect plan-violating hallucinations. We instantiate GC-DPG on a large Chinese Disease KG and evaluate it on a disease-centric QA dataset. Empirical results show that GC-DPG substantially improves entity-level precision and reduces hallucinations compared to strong KG-RAG and LLM-only baselines, indicating that explicit graph-based planning and guardrails are crucial for making LLM-based medical QA both accurate and verifiable.

titulo: Augmenting Small Language Model for Better Medical Question Answering through Source Authentication
autores: Das, Sourav; Chatterji, Sanjay; Mukherjee, Imon
venue: ACM Trans. Inf. Syst.
abstract: Medical question answering (QA) systems require both factual reliability and computational efficiency for real-world deployment. We address this dual challenge by introducing a resource-constrained framework that integrates a fine-tuned 1.5B-parameter Small Language Model with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and a calibrated fact-checking module specifically optimized for medical domain constraints. Our key contribution lies not merely in component integration, but in demonstrating how internal system metrics, particularly our Factual Consistency Score (FCS) serve as effective Query Performance Prediction (QPP) indicators for answer reliability in complex RAG pipelines, a critical gap in current IR paradigms. Evaluated on PubMedQA and standard medical benchmarks, our approach achieves competitive performance while operating on a single T4 GPU with a 7 GB memory footprint, requiring 85\% fewer resources than comparable 7B-parameter medical LLMs. The framework reduces hallucinations by 37\% (measured by FCS) compared to non-fact-checked baselines, though it currently has limitations in handling multi-hop medical reasoning and cross-sentence verification. Our work provides a practical blueprint for developing accessible, trustworthy medical QA systems that balance performance with infrastructure constraints, establishing that internal consistency metrics can effectively predict answer quality where traditional QPP methods fall short. The implementation demonstrates that resource-constrained environments need not sacrifice reliability when thoughtfully designed verification mechanisms are integrated into the retrieval-generation pipeline.

titulo: Design of an Intelligent Question Answering System for Universities Integrating Knowledge Graphs and Large Language Models
autores: Zhang, Jianli; Liu, Qian
venue: Proceedings of the 3rd International Conference on Educational Digitalization and Computer Science in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area
abstract: To address the problems of low factual accuracy, poor knowledge timeliness, and insufficient complex reasoning capability in question answering systems for university information services, this paper designs and implements an intelligent university question answering system that integrates knowledge graphs with large language models. The system constructs a university-domain knowledge graph comprising 1,847 entity nodes, 16 relation types, and 4,231 relation edges, covering four sub-domains: academic affairs, student status management, scholarships and financial aid, and career guidance. At the system design level, a hybrid retrieval strategy based on question intent classification is proposed, categorizing questions into three types — factual, explanatory, and procedural — and applying three distinct processing pipelines: Cypher-based precise querying, multi-hop subgraph retrieval, and procedural step injection, thereby avoiding the performance loss associated with a unified strategy. At the answer quality control level, two mechanisms are designed: empty-retrieval interception before generation and key numerical verification after generation, keeping the hallucination rate within an acceptable range. Experiments are conducted on an evaluation set of 500 real student consultation questions, comparing against four baselines: TF-IDF retrieval, BERT-FAQ matching, pure LLM generation, and document retrieval-augmented generation. Results show that the system achieves an exact match rate of 0.623 and a factual accuracy of 0.871, outperforming all baselines. Ablation experiments validate the individual contributions of three core modules: intent classification, structured graph querying, and answer verification. The system's average response time is 2.3 seconds with an answer cache hit rate of approximately 23\%, demonstrating practical feasibility for real university deployment.

titulo: Integrating Access Control with Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Proof of Concept for Managing Sensitive Patient Profiles
autores: Chen, Bingxiang; Tackman, John; Set\"al\"a, Manu; Poranen, Timo; Zhang, Zheying
venue: Proceedings of the 40th ACM/SIGAPP Symposium on Applied Computing
abstract: With advancements in Generative AI, particularly large language models (LLMs), there is significant potential for developing domain-specific AI chatbots. However, training on sensitive data, such as healthcare information, poses risks of unauthorized data leakage. Access control is essential to ensure that only authorized personnel can access sensitive training documents. This study proposes integrating fine-grained access control with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), a promising architecture that enables models to retrieve external data and generate contextually accurate responses. By combining RAG with access control, Generative AI can produce answers strictly based on documents permitted by user rights. This is particularly critical in healthcare, where only authorized personnel, such as doctors and nurses involved in treatment, should access patient-specific information. Using the design science research methodology, we developed a proof-of-concept system and evaluated it with patient profiles and varying access permissions. While not solving all data management challenges, this approach offers a promising solution for secure, domain-specific knowledge applications within LLMs.

titulo: Cross-Data Knowledge Graph Construction for LLM-enabled Educational Question-Answering System: A Case Study at HCMUT
autores: Bui, Tuan; Tran, Oanh; Nguyen, Phuong; Ho, Bao; Nguyen, Long; Bui, Thang; Quan, Tho
venue: Proceedings of the 1st ACM Workshop on AI-Powered Q&A Systems for Multimedia
abstract: In today's rapidly evolving landscape of Artificial Intelligence, large language models (LLMs) have emerged as a vibrant research topic. LLMs find applications in various fields and contribute significantly. Despite their powerful language capabilities, similar to pre-trained language models (PLMs), LLMs still face challenges in remembering events, incorporating new information, and addressing domain-specific issues or hallucinations. To overcome these limitations, researchers have proposed Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) techniques, some others have proposed the integration of LLMs with Knowledge Graphs (KGs) to provide factual context, thereby improving performance and delivering more accurate feedback to user queries.Education plays a crucial role in human development and progress. With the technology transformation, traditional education is being replaced by digital or blended education. Therefore, educational data in the digital environment is increasing day by day. Data in higher education institutions are diverse, comprising various sources such as unstructured/structured text, relational databases, web/app-based API access, etc. Constructing a Knowledge Graph from these cross-data sources is not a simple task. This article proposes a method for automatically constructing a Knowledge Graph from multiple data sources and discusses some initial applications (experimental trials) of KG in conjunction with LLMs for question-answering tasks.

titulo: Retrieval-Augmented Question Answering and Hallucination Mitigation for Theoretical Mechanics via the Synergy of Large Language Models and Knowledge Graphs
autores: Feng, Ning; Li, Yanjun; Wang, Houcheng; Cui, Junyi
venue: Proceedings of the 2nd International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Applications
abstract: As a core foundational course in engineering disciplines, theoretical mechanics exhibits a highly formalized and logically interconnected knowledge system. Traditional knowledge graph construction relies on manual annotation and expert ontology design, yet faces challenges such as high development costs, difficulties in iterative updates, and incomplete knowledge coverage. Systematic research on large language models (LLM)assisting automated knowledge graph construction in the field of mechanics remains limited. To address this, this paper proposes an LLM-enhanced knowledge graph question answering method based on subgraph-constrained reasoning. By explicitly modeling multi-hop paths and critical semantic relationships, the approach enables structured reasoning and interpretable generation for complex mechanical problems. During the construction phase, an LLM-assisted human-in-the-loop semi-automatic workflow is designed to transform textbook texts into structured knowledge. This workflow leverages large language models to optimize entity boundary recognition and disambiguation, enabling efficient conversion of text into structured knowledge. The workflow also utilizes the Neo4j graph database for persistent knowledge storage and multi-source integration. In the application phase, this paper determines problem types based on the cosine similarity between query embeddings and category prototype vectors, employing a confidence threshold to minimize classification errors. Fact-based questions are directly answered through precise knowledge graph triplet retrieval, while reasoning and low-confidence questions utilize 1-hop to 2-hop knowledge subgraph retrieval, key relationship filtering, and thought-process prompts to generate subgraph constraints, thereby establishing an interpretable retrieval-enhanced generation framework for theoretical mechanics. The experimental results demonstrate that the constructed theoretical mechanics knowledge graph encompasses 96 core entities and 97 directed relationships. The proposed method achieved an F1 score of 0.9725 across 200 test cases and outperformed F1 performance than pure LLM, keyword search, and baseline RAG under the current experimental setting. These findings indicate that knowledge graph constraints, problem type discrimination, and subgraph retrieval mechanisms enhance the accuracy, completeness, and interpretability of theoretical mechanics Q&A systems. In addition, real-student question cases involving tipping stability and D'Alembert's principle further show that the generated answers can be traced to retrieved subgraph evidence, thereby reducing evidence-free generation in the tested concept-explanation and formula-reasoning scenarios. This work establishes an LLM-assisted, human-machine collaborative semi-automatic knowledge graph construction and intelligent Q&A implementation framework for specialized disciplines such as theoretical mechanics.

titulo: Design and Implementation of a Multimodal Intelligent Agent System for Vocational Education Policy Question Answering Based on MCP Protocol
autores: Jiang, Zhonghua; Huang, Hexiao; Jin, Qi
venue: Proceedings of the 2026 2nd International Conference on Digital Education and Information Technology
abstract: The interpretation of vocational education policies faces the challenge of “structural fragmentation of data.” Critical documents typically exist as unstructured PDFs, while key execution data—such as enrollment quotas and funding allocations—reside in dynamic web pages or independent databases. This multi-source heterogeneity often leads to factual hallucinations in general Large Language Models (LLMs). To address this, we propose a Hierarchical Cooperative Agent Architecture based on the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Unlike traditional monolithic Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) solutions, our system encapsulates Web Search, Local Document Parsing, and Text-to-SQL queries as standardized MCP tool services. Furthermore, a Finite State Machine (FSM) governs the interaction logic. By employing a hybrid intent routing algorithm, the system implements a weighted evidence fusion mechanism. This mechanism achieves precise de-duplication when semantic conflicts arise between real-time Web streams and local knowledge bases. Fine-tuning experiments on the Qwen3 model demonstrate that our system significantly outperforms state-of-the-art general LLMs (e.g., GPT-4o, Qwen-2-72B) and mainstream agent frameworks in accuracy and logical coherence, particularly in tasks involving complex tabular reasoning. Extensive stress testing further confirms the system's robustness under high concurrency, demonstrating its feasibility for large-scale deployment.

titulo: Low-Hallucination RAG for Mathematical Question Answering: A Trustworthy Generation Method Based on Retrieval Hygiene, Step-Tree Reasoning, and Symbolic-Solver Feedback
autores: Wang, Jue
venue: Proceedings of the 2026 2nd International Conference on Generative Artificial Intelligence and Digital Media
abstract: Despite the remarkable advancements of Large Language Models (LLMs), their application in the mathematical domain is frequently hindered by “hallucinations,” characterized by logical inconsistencies, numerical fabrication, and the inability to handle under-constrained problems. This paper presents a robust mathematical reasoning framework that integrates Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with a symbolic verification engine to mitigate these issues. Our system addresses the limitations of purely probabilistic generation by implementing a proximity-based filtering mechanism and Maximal Marginal Relevance (MMR) reranking, ensuring high-fidelity knowledge retrieval. The core of our approach lies in a “Step-tree” reasoning architecture, where natural language derivations are structurally decomposed and cross-verified against a SymPy-driven symbolic engine. We introduce a recursive back-filling verification mechanism that ensures consistency between linguistic steps and deterministic computational results. Furthermore, a robust rejection gate is implemented to detect and refuse under-constrained queries, preventing the model from improvising non-existent conditions. Experimental evaluations were conducted on a curated dataset of 300 problems across primary, junior, and senior high school levels. The results demonstrate that the proposed system significantly outperforms vanilla LLM baselines, achieving a substantial reduction in the Hallucination Rate (HR) for insufficient queries. This research provides a verifiable and interpretable pathway for deploying large language models in high-precision educational and scientific applications.

titulo: Design and Empirical Analysis of an Intelligent Teaching Framework for Probability Theory and Mathematical Statistics Based on the DeepSeek Large Language Model
autores: Lv, Ning; Zou, Shengyong; Chen, Junlin; Wei, Fanrui
venue: Proceedings of the 3rd International Conference on Educational Digitalization and Computer Science in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area
abstract: To address the challenges of conceptual abstraction and limited classroom interaction in Probability Theory and Mathematical Statistics, this paper proposes a DeepSeek-based intelligent teaching framework. The framework consists of three layers, namely cognitive support, modeling training, and application expansion, and supports students through intelligent question answering, case-based guidance, and computational experiments. A teaching case on the binomial distribution was designed to demonstrate the implementation of the framework, and a quasi-experimental study was conducted in four parallel classes from the same major to compare the DeepSeek-assisted teaching mode with the traditional teaching mode. The results show that the experimental group achieved significantly better overall performance in the final examination, particularly in comprehensive application problems, and also demonstrated improvements in classroom interaction, question quality, and online learning engagement. These findings indicate that the proposed framework can enhance concept understanding, learning engagement, and comprehensive application ability. This study provides an empirically grounded reference for the teaching reform of Probability Theory and Mathematical Statistics and offers a practical model for other courses with highly abstract content.

titulo: CourseSeek: A Retrieval-Augmented Teaching Assistant for Instrumentation Education Based on a Distilled DeepSeek-R1 Model
autores: Zhu, Zeyuan; Wang, Yaobin; Yin, Xianhua; Zhu, Siyuan; Yang, Wenhao
venue: Proceedings of the 3rd International Conference on Educational Digitalization and Computer Science in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in natural language understanding and generation, offering new possibilities for the development of intelligent instructional systems in engineering education. However, when directly applied to undergraduate instrumentation education, general-purpose LLMs often suffer from insufficient domain knowledge coverage, inconsistent use of technical terminology, and limited support for experimental and engineering procedures. These limitations become more pronounced in teaching tasks that involve integrating knowledge across courses. To address these challenges, this paper proposes CourseSeek, a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system designed for undergraduate instrumentation education. The system adopts the lightweight DeepSeek-R1-Distill-14B model as the core generative component and constructs a domain-specific vector knowledge base from instrumentation textbooks, lecture materials, and laboratory manuals. By integrating relevant instructional knowledge during the generation process through an RAG mechanism, the system enhances domain adaptability and factual grounding. Experimental results demonstrate that, under the same model scale, incorporating a domain-specific RAG knowledge base leads to consistent improvements in terminology accuracy, conceptual completeness, and pedagogical usability. The findings indicate that the combination of a lightweight large language model and domain knowledge augmentation provides a feasible solution for deploying question-answering systems in real-world instrumentation education environments.

titulo: “There Are Things I Can’t Ask People”: User Perceptions of LLM-Based Chatbot for Sexual and Reproductive Health in India
autores: Moin, Sara; Himani; Singh, Pushpendra
venue: Proceedings of the 2026 ACM SIGCAS/SIGCHI Conference on Computing and Sustainable Societies
abstract: The rapid growth of large language models (LLMs) is reshaping access to health information, yet their role in sexual and reproductive health (SRH)—a highly stigmatized and sensitive domain is a nascent area of research, particularly in the Indian context. This study investigates how individuals perceive and engage with an LLM-based chatbot for SRH, examining trust boundaries, privacy expectations, and the cultural dimensions of LLM-mediated health communication. We designed a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) chatbot for sexual health and conducted a user study in which fifteen participants interacted with the system, followed by semi-structured interviews. Our findings reveal three interconnected themes: First, LLMs serve as low-stakes knowledge companions that reduce the cognitive and social burden of SRH information-seeking; secondly, privacy needs are relational and situational rather than uniform, shaped by domestic contexts and family structures; and lastly, LLM responses exhibit systematic gender bias in SRH framing—a pattern which carries significant implications for equitable chatbot design. We contribute design recommendations for culturally sensitive, privacy-aware, and gender-equitable LLM systems for SRH communication.

titulo: Academic Advising Chatbot Powered with AI Agent
autores: Tamascelli, Michael; Bunch, Olivia; Fowler, Blake; Taeb, Maryam; Cohen, Achraf
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 ACM Southeast Conference
abstract: Academic advising plays a crucial role in fostering student success. However, challenges such as limited advisor availability can hinder effective support. Generative AI, particularly AI-powered chatbots, offers the potential to enhance student advising in higher education by providing personalized guidance. These technologies help college students find the information and resources needed to create degree plans aligned with their academic goals. This research introduces ARGObot, an intelligent advising system that facilitates student navigation of university policies through automated interpretation of the student handbook as its primary knowledge base. ARGObot enhances accessibility to critical academic policies and procedures, supporting incoming students' success through personalized guidance. Our system integrates a multifunctional agent enhanced by a Large Language Model (LLM). The architecture employs multiple external tools to enhance its capabilities: a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system accesses verified university sources; email integration facilitates Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) interaction; and a web search function expands the system's knowledge base beyond predefined constraints. This approach enables the system to provide contextually relevant and verified responses to various student queries. This architecture evolved from our initial implementation based on Gemini 1 Pro, which revealed significant limitations due to its lack of agent-based functionality, resulting in hallucination issues and irrelevant responses. Subsequent evaluation demonstrated that our enhanced version, integrating GPT-4 with the text-embedding-ada-002 model, achieved superior performance across all metrics. This paper also presents a comparative analysis of both implementations, highlighting the architectural improvements and their impact on system performance.

titulo: Incorporating Graph-Constrained RAG Pipeline for Medicine data
autores: Verma, Shilpa; Sharma, Rishit
venue: Companion Proceedings of the ACM Web Conference 2026
abstract: Recent advancements in LLMs have transformed the research from a normal document-based search engine to a semantic-based contextual question-answering service. Understanding of relationships between the input query and related information is a crucial phase in this knowledge-extensive task. The aim of this paper is to engineer a knowledge graph-based LLM for scientific knowledge retrieval that adheres to fluent results with zero hallucinations. The proposed architecture incorporates the graph-constrained RAG pipeline, which is utilized as a natural language interface, whereas the knowledge graph is the mediator of facts and claims. We evaluated the proposed system on a curated dataset of samples, achieving retrieval precision of 71\% with accurate types of KG nodes. We discovered the hybrid system outperforms an individual LLM for all evaluation metrics.

titulo: NursingLLM: A Retrieval-Augmented Health Chatbot for Supporting Nursing Home Residents
autores: She, Dong; Ren, Junbin; Sun, Yueru; Zhang, Wenbo; Gao, Yang; Jin, Zhanpeng
venue: Companion of the 2025 ACM International Joint Conference on Pervasive and Ubiquitous Computing
abstract: Elderly individuals in nursing homes often experience loneliness and health-related anxiety. To explore how LLM-based chatbots might support this population, we conducted in-depth interviews with 23 elderly residents to understand their emotional and informational needs. Based on these findings, we designed and implemented NursingLLM, a conversational agent tailored for aging-related health support. Guided by principles from HCI and gerontology, the system emphasizes ease of use, trust-building, and empathetic interaction. NursingLLM integrates a multimodal (voice and text) interface to improve accessibility, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to provide verifiable health information, and prompting strategies to sustain natural and caring conversations. We then conducted a preliminary user study with 16 residents in two care centers to assess usability and perceived supportiveness. Results suggest that NursingLLM helped users better understand their symptoms, recall daily care routines, and feel more emotionally supported. This work offers design insights and a system prototype for future AI-driven tools to promote older adults' well-being in institutional settings.

titulo: JayBot -- Aiding University Students and Admission with an LLM-based Chatbot
autores: Odede, Julius; Frommholz, Ingo
venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Human Information Interaction and Retrieval
abstract: This demo paper presents JayBot, an LLM-based chatbot system aimed at enhancing the user experience of prospective and current students, faculty, and staff at a UK university. The objective of JayBot is to provide information to users on general enquiries regarding course modules, duration, fees, entry requirements, lecturers, internship, career paths, course employability and other related aspects. Leveraging the use cases of generative artificial intelligence (AI), the chatbot application was built using OpenAI’s advanced large language model (GPT-3.5 turbo); to tackle issues such as hallucination as well as focus and timeliness of results, an embedding transformer model has been combined with a vector database and vector search. Prompt engineering techniques were employed to enhance the chatbot’s response abilities. Preliminary user studies indicate JayBot’s effectiveness and efficiency. The demo will showcase JayBot in a university admission use case and discuss further application scenarios.

titulo: Designing an Embodied Chatbot for High School Students: An Interaction Analysis
autores: Holley, Christopher J.; Jamieson, Zan; Joshy, Ishaan; O'Leary, Brecken; Patel, Rohin; Sudula, Abhikruthi; Tenholder, Peter; Velagapudi, Anish; Hodges, Larry
venue: Proceedings of the 2026 ACM Southeast Conference
abstract: This paper presents DragonBot, an embodied retrieval augmented generation chatbot designed by high school students for use on their residential campus. The system combines a large language model with both static and dynamic institutional data to answer questions through a voice-based interface represented by an animated dragon mascot. DragonBot was deployed in a public student area for four days, during which 882 naturally occurring student questions were collected. Using a multistage human and LLM assisted coding process, the authors identified sixteen categories that reflect five broader themes: social interaction, campus life, requirements and rules, attempts to challenge the system, and miscellaneous queries. Response times and answer quality were also evaluated across static, dynamic, and model only inputs, showing that most answers were rated as helpful and that dynamic data produced the highest accuracy. The findings illustrate how high school students interact with an embodied agent in an authentic setting and provide initial evidence about the types of information they seek from such systems. This work contributes one of the first analyses of real world conversational data from a high school chatbot deployment.

titulo: Adaptive Multi-Agent Tutoring AI for Multimodal Mathematics Conversational Learning
autores: Le, Quy Minh; Nguyen, Hoang D.
venue: Proceedings of the 2nd ACM Workshop in AI-Powered Question \& Answering Systems
abstract: Providing tailored and multimodal academic support in mathematics remains a complex task, especially when the goal is to deliver timely assistance aligned with specific curricula. Many current question-answering (QA) systems are limited in interactivity, perform inconsistently across different input types (e.g., text, image, voice), and often fail to respond effectively to individual learning needs. These challenges are even more prominent in subjects like algebra or geometry, where abstract reasoning and step-by-step solutions are crucial. This paper introduces a conversational AI tutoring system grounded in Large Language Models (LLMs) and multi-agent design, with each agent addressing a specific instructional function (Informer, Verifier, Insight, Practice, Tutor). The system integrates multimodal inputs and features a personalized feedback loop that tracks student difficulties, updates learning records, and suggests suitable practice tasks or learning videos. Evaluated with ninth-grade students in Vietnam, the system has demonstrated promising results for both educational impact and broader applicability.

titulo: A Semantic-Adaptive Hybrid Retrieval Framework for the Education Domain
autores: Xiao, Wei; Wang, Kai; Feng, Aoran; Chen, Kunfang; Yu, Tai
venue: Proceedings of the 2026 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Digital Media and Education
abstract: Educational documents, such as textbooks and lecture notes, are characterized by strong logical structure, high contextual dependence, and a high density of technical terms. To address the fragmentation of contextual semantic information and the difficulty of matching key information when large language models (LLMs) are directly applied in the education domain, this paper proposes a semantic-adaptive hybrid retrieval framework for the education domain. First, instead of using traditional fixed-size chunking, the framework designs a dynamic semantic segmentation method based on embedding similarity. This method aims to identify the natural boundaries of knowledge units more accurately and to preserve the integrity of core theorems and principles in long-text derivation. Second, the framework constructs a dual-path hybrid retrieval mechanism that combines BM25-based sparse retrieval with BGE-M3-based dense retrieval, and introduces a Cross-Encoder module for multi-stage re-ranking. This design effectively balances exact matching of domain-specific symbols with the capture of deeper causal semantics. Experimental results show that the proposed framework achieves the best retrieval performance, with an NDCG@10 score of 0.9205. The findings validate the advantages of deterministic semantic segmentation and the proposed retrieval framework in the education domain, and provide an engineering practice paradigm and theoretical basis for building robust domain-specific LLM-based question-answering systems.

titulo: AutismCarebot: Emotion-First, Source-Aware Conversational Support for Autistic Users
autores: Srivastava, Shristi; Zolyomi, Annuska; Si, Dong
venue: Proceedings of the Extended Abstracts of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
abstract: Autistic people often seek support for stress regulation, communication challenges, and navigating services, yet general-purpose chatbots may miss neurodiversity-affirming language and can provide ungrounded advice. We present AutismCarebot, a web-based conversational agent that combines (1) an emotion-first response structure (validation, normalization, and a clear next step) with (2) retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to provide concise guidance grounded in curated autism resources with in-text citations. We designed the interaction to reduce cognitive load through quick prompts, progressive disclosure of detail, and a built-in “Take a Break” module offering guided breathing and grounding. We evaluated AutismCarebot through an automatic comparison with an unmodified large language model baseline and a survey study (n=18) including autistic adults, caregivers, educators, and students. Results indicate AutismCarebot produced more empathetic and better-grounded responses than the baseline, with no unsafe outputs observed in the audit. The survey feedback highlighted AutismCarebot's soothing tone, clarity, and practical advice, while emphasizing the necessity to control the level of links and provide multimodal support.

titulo: Method for Constructing TCM Syndrome Differentiation Q&A System with LLM-RAG
autores: Huang, Zhangfen; Zhao, Yun; Zhou, Yanjuan; Wang, Mingfeng; Li, Shenzhen; Sang, Ziyao; Shi, Chunchao
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 2nd Symposium on Big Data, Neural Networks, and Deep Learning
abstract: Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) represents a cornerstone of China's medical heritage, embodying millennia of clinical practice and accumulated therapeutic wisdom. As efforts to modernize TCM intensify, the demand for accurate, timely, and professionally informed responses to TCM-related inquiries has increased among clinicians, researchers, and the public. However, conventional TCM question-answering systems remain constrained by outdated knowledge bases, ambiguous interpretation of domain-specific terminology, and limited capacity for complex semantic reasoning. These shortcomings often result in imprecise or contextually inadequate answers. To overcome these challenges, this study introduces a question-answering framework based on Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), designed specifically for TCM applications. By integrating a curated TCM knowledge repository with the generative capabilities of large language models (LLMs) through a structured retrieval mechanism, the proposed system substantially improves the factual accuracy, contextual precision, and professional quality of generated responses.

titulo: Towards AI-Driven Academic Advising: Lessons from a Domain-Specific Implementation of a RAG-Based Chatbot
autores: Mendoza, Benito; Aktar, Afroza; Ahsan, Shajib; Yang, Kim; Zia, Farrukh; Ma, Lili; Wang, Yu; Kwon, Ohbong
venue: J. Comput. Sci. Coll.
abstract: Academic advising is essential for student success, but remains resource-intensive and difficult to scale. This paper presents a domain-specific implementation of an AI-powered advising chatbot based on a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture. The system combines vector-based document retrieval with a large language model (LLM) to deliver context-aware responses to course planning and policy-related queries. We evaluated the chatbot using 22 representative advising questions, rated by expert reviewers across four dimensions: Accuracy, Completeness, Clarity, and Policy Adherence. The system demonstrated strong performance in Clarity and Policy Adherence but struggled with complex scenarios that required prerequisite logic and multi-step reasoning. Reviewer feedback revealed common failure modes, including missing course dependencies and policy misalignment. These results highlight the potential and limitations of lightweight RAG-based advising tools, pointing to future improvements, including multi-agent designs, structured knowledge integration, and policy-aware reasoning.

titulo: HALO: Hallucination Analysis and Learning Optimization to Empower LLMs with Retrieval-Augmented Context for Guided Clinical Decision Making
autores: Anjum, Sumera; Zhang, Hanzhi; Zhou, Wenjun; Paek, Eun Jin; Zhao, Xiaopeng; Feng, Yunhe
venue: Proceedings of the ACM/IEEE International Conference on Connected Health: Applications, Systems and Engineering Technologies
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have significantly advanced natural language processing tasks, yet they are susceptible to generating inaccurate or unreliable responses, a phenomenon known as hallucination. In critical domains such as health and medicine, these hallucinations can pose serious risks. This paper introduces HALO, a novel framework designed to enhance the accuracy and reliability of medical question-answering (QA) systems by focusing on the detection and mitigation of hallucinations. Our approach generates multiple variations of a given query using LLMs and retrieves relevant information from external open knowledge bases to enrich the context. We utilize maximum marginal relevance scoring to prioritize the retrieved context, which is then provided to LLMs for answer generation, thereby reducing the risk of hallucinations. The integration of LangChain further streamlines this process, resulting in a notable and robust increase in the accuracy of both open-source and commercial LLMs, such as Llama-3.1 (from 44\% to 66\%) and ChatGPT (from 56\% to 70\%). This framework underscores the critical importance of addressing hallucinations in medical QA systems, ultimately improving clinical decision-making and patient care. The open-source HALO is available at: https://github.com/ResponsibleAILab/HALO.

titulo: Building a Voice-Activated RAG Chatbot with Generative AI and LLMs
autores: Wills, Tyler; Burgan, Cara; Guzide, Osman; Liao, Weidong
venue: J. Comput. Sci. Coll.
